outcome.en: State the law of conservation of energy and explain how energy changes forms
outcome.st: Hlalosa molao oa poloko ea matla le kamoo matla a fetohang mefuta

text.en: Energy is the ability to do work. The Law of Conservation of Energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another. For example, in a flashlight, chemical energy in the battery transforms into electrical energy, which then transforms into light and heat energy.
text.st: Matla ke bokhoni ba ho etsa mosebetsi. Molao oa Poloko ea Matla o re matla a ke ke a bōptjoa kapa a senngoa; a ka fetoloa feela ho tloha mofuteng o mong ho ea ho o mong. Mohlala, tocheng, matla a k'hemik'hale a betri a fetoha matla a motlakase, ao ka mor'a moo a fetohang matla a leseli le mocheso.

text.en: Have learners rub their hands together vigorously for 15 seconds. Ask: 'What energy did your moving hands have (kinetic)? What did you feel (heat)?'
text.st: Etsa hore baithuti ba hule matsoho a bona hammoho ka matla metsotsoana e 15. Botsa: 'Matsoho a neng a sisinyeha a ne a na le matla afe (kinetic)? U utloile eng (mocheso)?'

q.en: When hydropower at 'Muela generates electricity from falling water, kinetic energy is transformed into:
q.st: Ha motlakase oa metsi 'Muela o hlahisa motlakase ho tsoa metsing a phallang, matla a kinetic a fetoloa ho ba:

title.en: Renewable Energy: Solar, Wind, and Hydro in Lesotho
title.st: Matla a Tlhaho: Letsatsi, Moea, le Metsi Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Scientific & Technological Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Saense le Theknoloji

outcome.en: Evaluate renewable energy technologies suitable for rural electrification in Lesotho
outcome.st: Hlahloba theknoloji ea matla a letsatsi, moea le metsi e loketseng metse ea mahaeng

text.en: Renewable energy comes from natural resources that never run out. Lesotho has over 300 sunny days each year for solar power, strong mountain winds for wind turbines, and abundant highland water at ’Muela Hydropower Station to generate clean electricity without burning coal.
text.st: Matla a nchafalang a tsoa tlhahong ’me ha a fele. Lesotho le na le matsatsi a fetang 300 a letsatsi ka selemo bakeng sa motlakase oa letsatsi, meea e matla ea lithaba bakeng sa li-wind turbine, le metsi a mangata setsing sa motlakase sa ’Muela ho fehla motlakase o hloekileng.

text.en: Connect this to how solar lights allow learners in rural villages to study after dark without paraffin fumes.
text.st: Bapisang sena le kamoo mabone a letsatsi a thusang bana ba mahaeng ho ithuta bosiu ntle le mosi oa parafini.

q.en: Where is electricity generated from falling water inside Lesotho under the LHWP project?
q.st: Ke hokae moo motlakase o fehloang ka metsi a phallang ka hare ho Lesotho tlas'a morero oa LHWP?

options.st: Sebaka sa Lifofane sa Qacha’s Nek

title.st: Bongoli ba Bacha, Boikemelo, le Bohloeki

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Scientific & Technological Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Saense le Theknoloji

outcome.en: Understand physical and emotional changes during puberty with dignity and hygiene
outcome.st: Utloisisa liphetoho tsa ’mele le maikutlo nakong ea bocha ka seriti le bohloeki

text.en: Puberty is the transition period when a child develops into an adult. Physical changes include voice deepening, growth spurts, body hair, and menstruation for girls. Practicing good hygiene, respecting your body, and understanding these natural changes builds self-confidence.
text.st: Bochaba ke nako eo ngoana a fetohang ho ba motho e moholo. Liphetoho li kenyelletsa ho teba ha lentsoe, ho hola ka potlako, moriri ’meleng, le matsatsi a khoeli ho banana. Ho hlokomela bohloeki le ho hlompha ’mele oa hao ho haha boits'epo.

text.en: Encourage an open, supportive atmosphere where biological facts dispel fear, teasing, or cultural taboos.
text.st: Thehang moea o tletseng tšebelisano ’moho le tlhompho moo linnete tsa saense li felisang tšabo le ho tšeana.

q.en: Why do young people experience bodily and emotional changes during adolescence?
q.st: Hobaneng ha bacha ba ba le liphetoho tsa ’mele le maikutlo nakong ea bocha?

options.en: It is a normal, healthy biological process caused by hormones
options.st: Ke tšebetso e tloaelehileng le e phetseng hantle ea lihomone

options.en: It is a dangerous illness that requires hospital medicine
options.st: Ke boloi kapa bokuli bo kotsi

options.en: It only happens to children who misbehave
options.st: Ho etsahala feela ho bana ba sa mameleng

title.st: Litho tsa Lelapa la Ka

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Identify roles of family members and practice respect at home
outcome.st: Tseba mesebetsi ea litho tsa lelapa le ho bontša tlhompho lapeng

text.en: A family cares for and protects each other. In our homes, we have parents, grandparents (nkhono le ntate-moholo), brothers, and sisters. We show love by helping with simple chores like fetching water or sweeping the yard.
text.st: Lelapa le hlokomelana le ho sireletsana. Malapeng a rona, re na le batsoali, nkhono le ntate-moholo, bo-abuti le bo-ausi. Re bontša lerato ka ho thusa mesebetsing e kang ho kha metsi kapa ho fiela lebala.

text.en: Ask learners to draw a picture of their family doing an activity together at home.
text.st: Kopang baithuti ho taka setšoantšo sa lelapa la bona le sebetsa ’moho lapeng.

q.en: How can young children show love and respect to elders at home?
q.st: Bana ba banyenyane ba ka bontša lerato le tlhompho joang ho batho ba baholo lapeng?

options.en: By greeting politely and helping with chores
options.st: Ka ho lumelisa ka tlhompho le ho thusa mesebetsing
Ka ho baleha ha ba bitsoa
Ka ho hana ho ja lijo

title.st: Melao le Tšireletseho Sekolong

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Follow basic school safety guidelines and cooperate with classmates
outcome.st: Latela melao ea mantlha ea tšireletseho sekolong le ho sebelisana le bana ba bang

text.en: Our school is a place of learning and friendship. We obey school rules: we walk without running in corridors, we listen to our teachers, we do not push others, and we keep the schoolyard clean.
text.st: Sekolo sa rona ke sebaka sa ho ithuta le botsoalle. Re mamela melao ea sekolo: ha re mathe liphasejeng, re mamela matichere, ha re sutumetsane, ’me re hloekisa lebala la sekolo.

text.en: Role-play how to walk calmly in single file when entering the classroom.
text.st: Bapallang kamoo bana ba kenang ka molula-ho-ho-ea ka phaposing ntle le pherekano.

q.en: What should you do if you see banana peels or plastic trash in the school yard?
q.st: U lokela ho etsa eng ha u bona makhapetla a libanana kapa lipolastiki lebaleng la sekolo?

options.en: Pick it up and place it in the rubbish bin
options.st: E nke ’me u e lahle ka moqomong oa lithōle

options.en: Kick it further into the playground
options.st: E rahe e kene lebaleng la lipapali

options.en: Leave it there for animals to eat
options.st: E tlohele e jeoe ke liphoofolo

title.st: Libaka tsa Bohlokoa Motseng oa Rona

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Name key landmarks in the village such as the chief’s place, church, and water pump
outcome.st: Tseba libaka tsa bohlokoa motseng joaloka khotla, kereke, le pompo ea metsi

text.en: Every village in Lesotho has special places that serve our community: the Chief's court (lekhotleng) for community meetings, the clinic for healing sick people, the church for worship, and the community water tap.
text.st: Motse o mong le o mong Lesotho o na le libaka tsa bohlokoa: khotla la Morena bakeng sa liphutheho, tleliniki ea batho ba kulang, kereke ea thapelo, le pompo ea metsi ea sechaba.

text.en: Ask learners which landmark is closest to their home.
text.st: Botsang baithuti hore na ke sebaka sefe sa bohlokoa se haufi le malapa a bona.

q.en: Where do community elders and village members gather to discuss village safety and development?
q.st: Batho ba baholo le litho tsa motse ba bokana kae ho buisana ka tšireletseho le tsoelopele ea motse?

options.en: At the Chief’s court (Lekhotleng la Morena)
Behind the cattle kraal at night
At the football pitch during a match
options.st: Lebaleng la bolo nakong ea papali

title.st: Libaka sechabeng

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Understand core concepts of Places in a community
outcome.st: Utloisisa lintlha tsa sehlooho tsa thuto ena

text.en: A community is a group of people who live and work together. Our school, clinic and church are places in a community.
text.st: Sechaba ke sehlopha sa batho ba lulang le ho sebetsa hammoho. Sekolo, tleliniki le kereke ke libaka sechabeng.

text.en: Walk around the school yard and name the places learners know in their village.
text.st: Tsamaea lebaleng la sekolo ’me le rete libaka tseo bana ba li tsebang motseng.

q.en: Which is a place in a community?
q.st: Ke sebaka sefe sechabeng?

title.st: Tsela eo Batho ba Tsamaeang ka Eona Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Compare traditional transport (horses, walking) with modern transport (taxis, buses)
outcome.st: Bapisa lipalangoang tsa khale (lipere, maoto) le tsa morao-rao (litaxi, libese)

text.en: In the high mountains of Lesotho, people rely on horses and walking along footpaths. In towns like Maseru and Leribe, people travel using minibuses (4+1 taxis), large buses, and trucks.
text.st: Lithabeng tse phahameng tsa Lesotho, batho ba tsamaea ka lipere le ka maoto litselaneng. Litoropong tse kang Maseru le Leribe, batho ba palama li-taxi tsa 4+1, libese tse kholo, le literaka.

text.en: Discuss road safety when walking along tarred roads and looking both ways before crossing.
text.st: Buisanang ka tšireletseho litseleng le ho qamaka mahlakore ka bobeli pele u tšela tsela.

q.en: Why are Basotho ponies well-suited for traveling in the rugged highlands?
q.st: Hobaneng ha lipere tsa Basotho li loketse ho tsamaea lithabeng tse phahameng?

options.en: They are sure-footed, strong, and endure cold mountain weather
options.st: Li na le maoto a tiileng, li matla ebile li mamella serame

options.en: They can fly across wide rivers
options.st: Li khona ho fofa holim'a linoka

title.en: The Basotho Blanket (Kobo) and Mokorotlo Hat
title.st: Kobo ea Sesotho le Mokorotlo

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Identify the significance of the Basotho blanket and conical straw hat as national heritage
outcome.st: Tseba bohlokoa ba kobo ea Sesotho le mokorotlo e le lefa la sechaba

text.en: The Basotho blanket (kobo) is our national garment worn with pride for warmth and during ceremonies like weddings. The mokorotlo is a conical grass hat woven from local mosea grass, inspired by the shape of Mount Qiloane.
text.st: Kobo ea Sesotho ke seaparo sa boikhohomoso sa naha se aparaeng bakeng sa mofuthu le meletlong e kang ea machato. Mokorotlo ke katiba ea joang bo bitsoang mosea, e bōpiloeng ka sebopeho sa Thaba ea Qiloane.

text.en: Show a picture of Mount Qiloane next to a mokorotlo to highlight the iconic silhouette.
text.st: Bontšang setšoantšo sa Thaba ea Qiloane pel'a mokorotlo ho bona tšoano ea tsona.

q.en: Which famous mountain near Thaba-Bosiu gave shape and inspiration to the national hat (Mokorotlo)?
q.st: Ke thaba efe e tsebahalang haufi le Thaba-Bosiu e faneng ka sebopeho sa katiba ea naha (Mokorotlo)?

title.st: Litereke Tse 10 tsa Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Name and locate the 10 administrative districts of Lesotho on a map
outcome.st: Reha le ho fumana litereke tse 10 tsa tsamaiso tsa Lesotho ’mapeng

text.en: The Kingdom of Lesotho is divided into 10 districts: Maseru (the capital), Berea, Leribe, Butha-Buthe, Mokhotlong, Thaba-Tseka, Qacha's Nek, Quthing, Mohale's Hoek, and Mafeteng. Each district has a administrative town.
text.st: ’Muso oa Lesotho o arotsoe ka litereke tse 10: Maseru (motse-moholo), Berea, Leribe, Butha-Buthe, Mokhotlong, Thaba-Tseka, Qacha's Nek, Quthing, Mohale's Hoek, le Mafeteng. Setereke ka seng se na le toropo ea tsamaiso.

text.en: Have learners chant the 10 districts starting from the north down to the south.
text.st: Etsang hore baithuti ba bine mabitso a litereke ho tloha leboea ho ea boroa.

q.en: Which district is the capital city and center of government in Lesotho?
q.st: Ke setereke sefe se nang le motse-moholo le setsi sa mebuso Lesotho?

title.st: Linako Tse ’Nè tsa Selemo Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Describe farming and clothing practices during the four distinct seasons
outcome.st: Hlalosa mesebetsi ea temo le liaparo linakong tse nne tsa selemo

text.en: Lesotho has four seasons: Spring (Selemo) when farmers plough and flowers bloom; Summer (Lehlabula) with rains and growing crops; Autumn (Hoetla) when maize is harvested; and Winter (Mariha) with frost, cold winds, and snow on the mountains.
text.st: Lesotho le na le linako tse ’nè: Selemo (balemi ba lema, lipalesa lia thunya); Lehlabula (pula ea na, lijalo lia hola); Hoetla (ho kotuloa poone le mabele); le Mariha (serame se bohale, moea o batang le lehloa lithabeng).

text.en: Discuss how herdboys prepare heavy gumboots, thick blankets, and balaclavas for winter.
text.st: Buisanang ka kamoo balisana ba itokisetsang mariha ka likobo tse tenya, likatiba le lijalane.

q.en: During which season do Basotho farmers harvest dry maize, beans, and pumpkins from fields?
q.st: Ke nakong efe ea selemo moo balemi ba Basotho ba kotulang poone, linaoa le maphodi masimong?

title.en: Morabaraba, Liketo, and Melao ea Tsona
title.st: Morabaraba, Liketo, le Melao ea Tsona

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Explain the rules of Morabaraba and how it teaches patience and strategic thinking
outcome.st: Hlalosa melao ea Morabaraba le kamoo e rutang mamello le bohlale ba maano

text.en: Morabaraba is an ancient traditional board game played on carved rock or cardboard with 12 cows (tokens) each. It teaches planning, counting, and strategic defense. Liketo is a hand-eye coordination game played with small stones and a hole in the ground.
text.st: Morabaraba ke papali ea bohlale ea khale e bapaloang lefikeng kapa khatoneng e nang le likhomo tse 12 ka lehlakore. E ruta moralo, lipalo, le tšireletso. Liketo ke papali ea matsoho le mahlo e bapaloang ka majoana le sekoti fatše.

text.en: Draw a Morabaraba board in the sand outside and let two learners play a quick match.
text.st: Ralang Morabaraba mobung lebaleng ebe le lumella baithuti ba babeli ho bapala papali e potlakileng.

q.en: How many cows (tokens) does each player start with in the game of Morabaraba?
q.st: Sebapali ka seng se qala ka likhomo (majoe) tse kae papaling ea Morabaraba?

title.en: Thaba-Bosiu: The Mountain Fortress of Peace
title.st: Thaba-Bosiu: Qhobosheane ea Khotso

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Describe how King Moshoeshoe I used Thaba-Bosiu to defend and unite the Basotho nation
outcome.st: Hlalosa kamoo Morena Moshoeshoe I a sebelisitseng Thaba-Bosiu ho sireletsa le ho kopanya sechaba

text.en: In 1824, King Moshoeshoe I led his people from Butha-Buthe to Thaba-Bosiu ("Mountain at Night"). With sheer cliffs and natural passes like Khubelu and Raebe, it could be defended easily. On top, fertile soil and spring water kept people alive during sieges.
text.st: Ka 1824, Morena Moshoeshoe I o ile a etella sechaba pele ho tloha Butha-Buthe ho ea Thaba-Bosiu ("Thaba ea Bosiu"). Ka mafika a eona a phahameng le likhoro tse kang Khubelu le Raebe, e ne e le thata ho hlaseloa. Holimo ho ne ho na le mehloli ea metsi le makhulo.

text.en: Emphasize Moshoeshoe’s philosophy of peace ("Khotso ke khoro") rather than warfare.
text.st: Totobatsang mohopolo oa Morena Moshoeshoe oa khotso ("Khotso ke khoro") ho e-na le ntoa.

q.en: Why was Thaba-Bosiu such an effective stronghold for King Moshoeshoe I?
q.st: Hobaneng ha Thaba-Bosiu e ne e le qhobosheane e matla hakaale bakeng sa Morena Moshoeshoe I?

options.en: Steep natural cliffs and freshwater springs on top
options.st: Mafika a phahameng a tlhaho le mehloli ea metsi a hloekileng holimo
E ne e na le literata tsa motlakase

options.en: It was surrounded by sea water
options.st: E ne e pota-potiloe ke metsi a leoatle

title.st: Kauta e Tšoeu: Metsi a Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Explain why water is referred to as Lesotho’s "White Gold"
outcome.st: Hlalosa lebaka leo ka lona metsi a bitsoang "Kauta e Tšoeu" ea Lesotho

text.en: Water is our most valuable natural resource, nicknamed "White Gold". Lesotho's high mountains receive heavy rainfall and snow. Through the Lesotho Highlands Water Project (Katse and Mohale dams), water is delivered to South Africa, earning revenue for our country.
text.st: Metsi ke sesebelisoa sa bohlokoa ka ho fetisisa Lesotho, ’me a bitsoa "Kauta e Tšoeu". Lithaba tsa Maloti li fumana pula le lehloa le lengata. Ka Morero oa Metsi a Lihlaba (Katse le Mohale), metsi a romeloa Afrika Boroa, ho kenya chelete sechabeng sa rona.

text.en: Show photos or map locations of Katse Dam wall, which is over 185 metres high.
text.st: Bontšang setšoantšo kapa sebaka sa letamo la Katse leo lerako la lona le fetang bophahamo ba limithara tse 185.

q.en: Why is water from Lesotho’s highlands called "White Gold"?
q.st: Hobaneng ha metsi a lithaba tsa Lesotho a bitsoa "Kauta e Tšoeu"?

options.en: It is a pure, clean resource that generates national income
options.st: Ke sesebelisoa se hloekileng se kenyang chelete e ngata naheng

options.en: Because it turns white when exposed to sunlight
options.st: Hobane a fetoha a masoeu letsatsing

options.en: Because real gold is dissolved inside it
options.st: Hobane a na le kauta ea ’nete ka hare

title.st: Ho Thibela Likhohlo le Khoholeho ea Mobu

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Identify causes of soil erosion and community actions to prevent dongas
outcome.st: Tseba lisosa tsa khoholeho ea mobu le mekhoa ea sechaba ea ho thibela likhohlo

text.en: Soil erosion is a serious threat in Lesotho. When slopes are overgrazed or trees are chopped down, heavy rainwater washes topsoil away, creating massive ravines (dongas). Planting vetiver grass, planting trees, and building stone check-dams heal the land.
text.st: Khoholeho ea mobu ke bothata bo boholo Lesotho. Ha makhulo a jeoa ho feta tekanyo kapa lifate li rengoa, pula e matla e hohola mobu o motle ebe e etsa likhohlo tse kholo. Ho lema lifate, joang le ho haha methinya ea majoe ho pholosa naha.

text.en: Take learners to observe a small gully near the school and discuss how stone barriers slow rushing water.
text.st: Etsang leeto ho ea bona khohloana e haufi le sekolo le ho buisana kamoo lirapa tsa majoe li emisang lebelo la metsi.

q.en: What can communities plant on bare hillsides to bind soil and stop donga formation?
q.st: Sechaba se ka lema eng matsoapong a se nang letho ho tšoara mobu le ho emisa likhohlo?

options.en: Deep-rooted grass, shrubs, and indigenous trees
options.st: Joang bo metse e tebileng le lifate tsa tlhaho
Ha ho letho, mobu o sa lengoang o molemo

title.en: King Moshoeshoe I and the Founding of Lesotho
title.st: Morena Moshoeshoe I le Ho Thehoa ha Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 5 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 5 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Describe how King Moshoeshoe I united different clans to found the Basotho nation
outcome.st: Hlalosa kamoo Morena Moshoeshoe I a kopantseng mefuta e fapaneng ho theha sechaba sa Basotho

text.en: King Moshoeshoe I was born around 1786 at Menkhoaneng. During a time of great conflict known as the Lifaqane, he led his people to the fortress of Thaba Bosiu in 1824. Through diplomacy, wisdom, and peace rather than warfare alone, he welcomed refugees from different clans and united them into one nation: the Basotho. His famous motto was 'Khotso ke khoro' (Peace is the mother of prosperity).
text.st: Morena Moshoeshoe I o hlahile hoo e ka bang ka 1786 Menkhoaneng. Nakong ea lintoa tse matla tse neng li bitsoa Lifaqane, o ile a etella batho ba hae pele ho ea qhobosheaneng ea Thaba Bosiu ka 1824. Ka bohlale, kgotso le ho arolelana ho e-na le lintoa feela, o ile a amohela baphaphathehi ba mefuta e fapaneng 'me a ba kopanya ho ba sechaba se le seng: Basotho. Polelo ea hae e tummeng e ne e le 'Khotso ke khomo ea lebenkele'.

text.en: Ask learners to gather in a circle and share one thing they know about Thaba Bosiu. Discuss why Moshoeshoe chose a mountain flat at the top with steep cliffs for his people's safety.
text.st: Kopa baithuti ho bokeletsa sedikong 'me ba arolelane ntho e le 'ngoe eo ba e tsebang ka Thaba Bosiu. Buisanang ka lebaka leo Moshoeshoe a kentseng thaba e bataletseng holimo e nang le mafika a motheo bakeng sa polokeho ea batho ba hae.

q.en: Which historic mountain fortress did King Moshoeshoe I choose as his capital in 1824?
q.st: Ke qhobosheana efe ea thaba ea nalane eo Morena Moshoeshoe I a e kentseng e le motse-moholo oa hae ka 1824?

title.st: Matšoao a Sechaba a Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 5 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 5 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Identify and explain the meaning of the flag, the Mokorotlo, and the Coat of Arms
outcome.st: Tseba le ho hlalosa moelelo oa folakha, Mokorotlo le Letšoao la Naha

text.en: Lesotho has national symbols that represent its unity and identity. The national flag has three horizontal stripes: blue (representing rain or 'Pula'), white (representing peace or 'Khotso'), and green (representing prosperity or 'Nala'). In the center of the white stripe is a black Mokorotlo (traditional Basotho conical grass hat). The national motto of Lesotho is 'Khotso, Pula, Nala' (Peace, Rain, Prosperity).
text.st: Lesotho le na le matšoao a sechaba a emelang bonngoe le boitsebahatso ba lona. Folakha ea naha e na le mebala e meraro e robaletseng: boputsoa (bo emelang 'Pula'), bosoeu (bo emelang 'Khotso'), le botala (bo emelang 'Nala'). Bohareng ba bosoeu ho na le Mokorotlo o motšo. Sepheo sa naha sa Lesotho ke 'Khotso, Pula, Nala'.

text.en: Have learners draw the national flag of Lesotho using crayons or coloured pencils. Make sure they place blue on top, white in the middle with the black Mokorotlo, and green at the bottom.
text.st: Lumella baithuti ho thala folakha ea naha ea Lesotho ba sebelisa mebala. Netefatsa hore ba beha boputsoa holimo, bosoeu bohareng bo nang le Mokorotlo o motšo, le botala tlase.

q.en: What do the three words in the national motto of Lesotho mean?
q.st: Mantsoe a mararo a sepheo sa naha sa Lesotho a bolela eng?

title.en: The Four Ecological Zones of Lesotho
title.st: Libaka tse 'Nè tsa Tlhaho tsa Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 5 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 5 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Identify and describe the Lowlands, Foothills, Highlands, and Senqu River Valley
outcome.st: Tseba le ho hlalosa Mabala, Lithota, Lithaba le Phula ea Noka ea Senqu

text.en: Lesotho is divided into four main geographical zones: (1) The Lowlands (Mabala) along the western border, where most people live and crop farming takes place; (2) The Foothills (Lithota), between the lowlands and the mountains, good for livestock grazing; (3) The Highlands (Lithaba / Maloti), covering more than two-thirds of the country with high mountain peaks; (4) The Senqu River Valley, a dry and warmer valley carved by the great Senqu River.
text.st: Lesotho le arotsoe ka libaka tse 'nè tse kholo tsa thuto ea lefats'e: (1) Mabala ka nqena e bophirima, moo batho ba bangata ba lulang le ho lema teng; (2) Lithota, pakeng tsa mabala le lithaba, tse loketseng phula ea liphoofolo; (3) Lithaba (Maloti), a koahelang karolo e fetang tse peli ho tse tharo tsa naha ka litlhoro tse telele; (4) Phula ea Noka ea Senqu, phula e omileng le e futhumetseng e fatiloeng ke Noka e kholo ea Senqu.

text.en: Show a map of Lesotho on the board. Point to Maseru, Leribe, and Mafeteng (Lowlands), Mokhotlong and Thaba-Tseka (Highlands), and ask learners which zone their school is located in.
text.st: Bonts'a 'mmapa oa Lesotho lebordong. Supa Maseru, Leribe, le Mafeteng (Mabala), Mokhotlong le Thaba-Tseka (Lithaba), ebe o botsa baithuti hore na sekolo sa bona se sebakeng sefe.

q.en: Which ecological zone covers the largest portion of Lesotho's total land area?
q.st: Ke sebaka sefe sa tlhaho se koahelang karolo e kholo ka ho fetisisa ea naha ea Lesotho?

title.en: Soil Erosion and Conserving Our Land (Mokhotha)
title.st: Khoholeho ea Mobu le Poloko ea Mobu (Mokhotha)

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 5 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 5 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Explain causes of soil erosion in Lesotho and ways to conserve the soil
outcome.st: Hlalosa lisosa tsa khoholeho ea mobu Lesotho le mekhoa ea ho sireletsa mobu

text.en: Soil is one of Lesotho's most precious natural resources. Soil erosion happens when wind and heavy summer rain wash away the rich topsoil, forming deep gullies called 'dongas' (mokhotha). Main causes include cutting down trees for firewood, overgrazing by too many livestock, and ploughing down slopes instead of across contours. We can prevent soil erosion by planting indigenous trees, making stone check dams in gullies, and practicing contour ploughing.
text.st: Mobu ke e 'ngoe ea lits'ebeletso tsa bohlokoa ka ho fetisisa tsa tlhaho Lesotho. Khoholeho ea mobu e etsahala ha moea le lipula tse matla tsa lehlabula li nka mobu o nonneng, li etsa likoti tse tebileng tse bitsoang mokhotha. Lisosa tse kholo li kenyelletsa ho rema lifate, ho fula haholo ha liphoofolo, le ho lema ka ho theoha leralleng ho e-na le ho lema ka li-contour. Re ka thibela sena ka ho lema lifate, ho haha mathata a majoe likoting, le ho lema ka ho potoloha maralla.

text.en: Take learners outside to look for a small donga or erosion patch on the school grounds. Have them place small stones across the water path to demonstrate how check-dams slow down running water.
text.st: Nka baithuti kantle ho batla mokhotha o monyenyane kapa sebaka se khoholehileng lebaleng la sekolo. Etsa hore ba behe majoe a manyenyane tseleng ea metsi ho bonts'a kamoo mathata a majoe a fokotsang lebelo la metsi.

q.en: What is an effective way to stop rainwater from washing away soil on steep slopes?
q.st: Ke mokhoa ofe o sebetsang oa ho thibela metsi a pula ho hohola mobu maralleng?

options.en: Ploughing along contours and planting trees
options.st: Ho lema ka li-contour le ho lema lifate

options.en: Letting more cattle graze on the slopes
options.st: Ho fepa likhomo tse ngata maralleng

title.st: Boetapele ba Setso le Puso ea Libaka

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 5 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 5 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Explain the role of the village chief (Morena) and community councils in Lesotho
outcome.st: Hlalosa karolo ea Morena oa motse le makhotla a libaka Lesotho

text.en: In Lesotho, communities are guided by both traditional leaders and elected local councils. The village chief (Morena) resolves disputes, witnesses agreements, ensures peace, and organizes communal work called 'matsema'. The village court or gathering place is called the 'Khotla'. Today, community councils work alongside chiefs to build water taps, repair roads, and maintain community clinics.
text.st: Lesotho, sechaba se tataisoa ke baetapele ba setso le makhotla a khethiloeng a libaka. Morena oa motse o rarolla liqabang, o paka litumellano, o tiisa khotso, le ho hlophisa mosebetsi oa sechaba o bitsoang 'matsema'. Lekhotla la motse kapa sebaka sa kopano se bitsoa 'Khotleng'. Kajeno, makhotla a libaka a sebetsa hammoho le marena ho kenya lipompo tsa metsi, ho lokisa litsela le ho hlokomela likliniki.

text.en: Conduct a mini 'Khotla' role-play in the classroom. Assign one learner to be the Chief, two to be elders, and two neighbors with a minor disagreement over garden boundaries. Let the Khotla listen and solve it peacefully.
text.st: Etsa papali ea 'Khotla' phapusing. Khetha moithuti a le mong ho ba Morena, ba babeli ho ba baholo, le baahelani ba babeli ba nang le khang e nyane ka meeli ea masimo. Lumella Khotla ho mamela le ho rarolla ka khotso.

q.en: What is the traditional name for the Basotho communal gathering and court place where village matters are discussed?
q.st: Lebitso la setso la sebaka sa kopano le lekhotla la Basotho moo litaba tsa motse li buisanoang teng ke lefe?

title.st: Morero oa Metsi a Lihlaba tsa Lesotho (LHWP)

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 5 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 5 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Describe the Katse Dam, electricity generation at 'Muela, and water transfer
outcome.st: Hlalosa Letamo la Katse, tlhahiso ea motlakase 'Muela le phetiso ea metsi

text.en: Water is known as the 'White Gold' of Lesotho. The Lesotho Highlands Water Project (LHWP) is one of the largest engineering projects in Africa. Massive dams like Katse Dam and Mohale Dam store water in the Maloti mountains. Underground tunnels transfer water northward to South Africa, earning revenue for Lesotho, while the rushing water drives turbines at the 'Muela Hydropower Station to generate electricity for Lesotho.
text.st: Metsi a tsebahala e le 'Khauta e Tšoeu' ea Lesotho. Morero oa Metsi a Lihlaba tsa Lesotho (LHWP) ke o mong oa merero e meholo ka ho fetisisa ea boenjiniere Afrika. Matamo a maholo a kang Letamo la Katse le Letamo la Mohale a boloka metsi lithabeng tsa Maloti. Likotopo tse ka tlas'a lefatše li isa metsi Afrika Boroa, ho fumanela Lesotho chelete, ha metsi a phallang a tsamaisa metšini ea motlakase seteisheneng sa 'Muela ho hlahisa motlakase bakeng sa Lesotho.

text.en: Show pictures of Katse Dam (the curved concrete wall) and explain how water pressure turns a waterwheel or turbine to make clean electricity.
text.st: Bonts'a litšoantšo tsa Letamo la Katse (lerako le kobehileng la konkreiti) 'me u hlalose kamoo matla a metsi a potolohang leoto la metsi kapa turbine ho etsa motlakase o hloekileng.

q.en: What valuable natural resource of Lesotho is often referred to as 'White Gold'?
q.st: Ke mohloli ofe oa bohlokoa oa tlhaho oa Lesotho o atisang ho bitsoa 'Khauta e Tšoeu'?

title.en: Constitutional Monarchy and Parliament of Lesotho
title.st: Borena le Paramente ea Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Explain the structure of Lesotho’s government including the King, Prime Minister, and Parliament
outcome.st: Hlalosa sebopeho sa puso ea Lesotho ho kenyeletsoa Morena, Tona-Kholo, le Paramente

text.en: Lesotho is a Constitutional Monarchy. His Majesty King Letsie III is the Head of State and symbol of national unity. The Head of Government is the Prime Minister, supported by Cabinet ministers. Laws are debated and passed by the National Assembly and the Senate.
text.st: Lesotho ke naha ea Borena ba Molao oa Motheo. Motlotlehi Morena Letsie III ke Hlooho ea Naha le letšoao la bonngoe ba sechaba. Hlooho ea Puso ke Tona-Kholo. Melao e sebetsoa le ho fetisoa ke Paramente (Lekhotla la Sechaba le Senate).

text.en: Organize a mock parliamentary debate in class on a village community issue.
text.st: Hlophisang ngangisano ea paramente phaposing ka taba e amang motse.

q.en: Who is the Head of State and symbol of national unity in the Kingdom of Lesotho?
q.st: Ke mang Hlooho ea Naha le letšoao la bonngoe ba sechaba ka hare ho ’Muso oa Lesotho?

title.en: Lesotho in SADC and the African Union
title.st: Lesotho ka hare ho SADC le Kopano ea Afrika (AU)

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Understand Lesotho’s role in regional trade, peace, and cultural cooperation
outcome.st: Utloisisa karolo ea Lesotho khoebong ea linaha, khotso, le tšebelisano ea setso

text.en: Lesotho is an active member of SADC (Southern African Development Community) and the African Union (AU). Being surrounded completely by South Africa, regional cooperation allows for open trade, road transit, labor migration, and peaceful regional security.
text.st: Lesotho ke setho se mafolofolo sa SADC le Mokhatlo oa Kopano ea Afrika (AU). Kaha le teetsoe hare ke Afrika Boroa, tšebelisano ena e lumella khoebo e lokolohileng, litsela, bafeti ba mesebetsi le tšireletso ea khotso.

text.en: Explain what an "enclave" country means and show a world map with Lesotho completely inside South Africa.
text.st: Hlalosang hore na naha e pota-potiloeng e bolela eng ’mapeng oa lefatše.

q.en: What unique geographic feature describes Lesotho on the African continent?
q.st: Ke sebopeho sefe sa lefatshe se khethehileng se hlalosang Lesotho kontinenteng ea Afrika?

options.en: It is an independent sovereign state completely encircled by South Africa
options.st: Ke naha e ikemetseng e teetsoeng hare ka ho felletseng ke Afrika Boroa

options.en: It is an island located in the Atlantic Ocean

options.st: E moeling le linaha tse hlano tse fapaneng

title.en: Children’s Rights and Protection in Lesotho
title.st: Litokelo tsa Bana le Tšireletso ea Bona Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: State basic children’s rights (education, health, safety) and corresponding duties
outcome.st: Tseba litokelo tsa mantlha tsa bana (thuto, bophelo bo botle, tšireletso) le mesebetsi ea bona

lessons.source: Lesotho Child Protection and Welfare Act / Curriculum

text.en: Under Lesotho law, every child has the right to free primary education, healthcare, shelter, a name, and protection from abuse or dangerous labor. With rights come responsibilities: to respect parents, attend school diligently, and treat others fairly.
text.st: Tlas'a molao oa Lesotho, ngoana e mong le e mong o na le tokelo ea thuto ea motheo ea mahala, kalafo, bolulo, lebitso, le tšireletso tlhekefetsong kapa mesebetsing e kotsi. Litokelo li tsamaea le boikarabello ba ho hlompha batsoali le ho kena sekolo.

text.en: Remind learners of Childline Lesotho (toll-free 116) as a safe channel if they face danger.
text.st: Hopotsang baithuti ka nomoro ea mahala ea Childline Lesotho (116) ha ba le kotsing.

q.en: Which of the following is a fundamental legal right guaranteed to children in Lesotho?
q.st: Har'a tse latelang, ke tokelo efe ea molao e netefalitsoeng ho bana ba Lesotho?

options.en: Right to free primary education and safety from exploitation
options.st: Tokelo ea thuto ea motheo ea mahala le tšireletso tlatlapong

options.en: Right to work in deep mines instead of school
options.st: Tokelo ea ho sebetsa merafong e tebileng ho e-na le ho kena sekolo

options.en: Right to harm others without consequence
options.st: Tokelo ea ho ntša ba bang kotsi ntle le kotlo

title.en: Pillars of the Lesotho Economy: Garments, Mining, and Agriculture
title.st: Litšiea tsa Moruo oa Lesotho: Liaparo, Merafo, le Temo

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Analyze key industries driving employment and trade in Lesotho
outcome.st: Hlahloba liindaseteri tse kholo tse fanang ka mesebetsi le khoebo Lesotho

text.en: The economy of Lesotho relies on four major sectors: Textile manufacturing in Maseru and Maputsoe (exporting clothing worldwide), diamond mining at Letseng and Kao, water and hydroelectric royalties from LHWP, and agriculture (wool, mohair, and crops).
text.st: Moruo oa Lesotho o itšetlehile ka likarolo tse ’nè tse kholo: Lifeme tsa liaparo Maseru le Maputsoe, merafo ea litaemane ea Letseng le Kao, tefo ea metsi le motlakase ea LHWP, le temo le leruo (boea le pholeche).

text.en: Mention that Letseng Mine is famous worldwide for producing some of the highest-value large white diamonds in history.
text.st: Bolelang hore Morafo oa Letseng o tumme lefatšeng ka ho hlahisa litaemane tse kholo ka ho fetisisa lefatšeng.

q.en: Which precious mineral mined in Lesotho’s Maloti mountains generates significant export value?
q.st: Ke moruo ofe oa tšepe ea bohlokoa o chekoang lithabeng tsa Maloti o tlisang chelete e ngata naheng?

title.st: Ho Falalla ho Tloha Mahaeng ho Ea Litoropong

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Explain the push and pull factors leading people to migrate from mountain villages to lowlands towns
outcome.st: Hlalosa mabaka a susumetsang batho ho tloha mahaeng a lithaba ho ea litoropong tsa mabalane

text.en: Many families migrate from rural mountain areas to towns like Maseru, Teyateyaneng, and Maputsoe. Push factors include lack of jobs, soil degradation, and harsh winters. Pull factors include tertiary colleges, factories, hospitals, and commercial services.
text.st: Malapa a mangata a falalla ho tloha mahaeng a lithaba ho ea litoropong tse kang Maseru le Maputsoe. Mabaka a ho tloha a kenyeletsa ho hloka mesebetsi le serame se bohale. Mabaka a ho hula a kenyeletsa likoleche, lifeme, le lipetlele tse kholo.

text.en: Lead a debate on whether young graduates should remain to modernize rural agriculture or seek urban employment.
text.st: Etsang ngangisano ea hore na bacha ba lokela ho sala mahaeng ho ntlafatsa temo kapa ho ea litoropong.

q.en: What is a major "pull factor" attracting young adults to lowlands cities in Lesotho?
q.st: Ke lebaka lefe le leholo le hulang bacha ho ea litoropong tsa mabalane Lesotho?

options.en: Higher education institutions and formal employment opportunities
options.st: Litsi tsa thuto e phahameng le menyetla ea mesebetsi

options.en: More open grazing pasture for cattle
Total absence of traffic or noise
options.st: Ho se be le sephethe-phethe ho hang

title.st: Lipheo tsa Ntlafatso e Tšoarellang (SDGs) Bakeng sa Lesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Social Sciences Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Disaense tsa Sechaba

outcome.en: Relate the UN SDGs (Quality Education, No Poverty, Clean Water) to local community development
outcome.st: Amanisa Lipheo tsa UN (Thuto ea Boleng, Ho Felisa Bofuma, Metsi a Hloekileng) le tsoelopele ea motse

lessons.source: United Nations / Lesotho National Strategic Plan

text.en: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals are 17 global goals to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure prosperity for all by 2030. In Lesotho, priority goals include SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 4 (Quality Education for every child), and SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation).
text.st: Lipheo tsa Ntlafatso e Tšoarellang tsa Machaba (SDGs) ke lipheo tse 17 tsa ho felisa bofuma le ho sireletsa polanete ka 2030. Lesotho, lipheo tsa mantlha li kenyeletsa SDG 1 (Ho Felisa Bofuma), SDG 4 (Thuto ea Boleng ho bana bohle), le SDG 6 (Metsi a Hloekileng le Bohloeki).

text.en: Connect this lesson directly to Moshoeshoe Hub app as a concrete local ICT4D contribution to SDG 4 and SDG 10.
text.st: Kopanyang thuto ena ka kotloloho le app ena ea Moshoeshoe Hub e le karolo ea tlatsetso ea ICT4D ho SDG 4 le SDG 10.

q.en: Which Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) focuses on ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education for all?
q.st: Ke Sepheo sefe sa Ntlafatso e Tšoarellang (SDG) se shebaneng le ho netefatsa thuto ea boleng bo phahameng bakeng sa bohle?

title.en: Alphabet Letter Sounds: A, B, C
title.st: Melumo ea Litlhaku: A, B, C

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Recognize the letters A, B, C and match them to simple words
outcome.st: Tseba litlhaku A, B, C le ho li bapisitse le mantsoe a bonolo

text.en: Every letter in English has a name and a sound. 'A' says /æ/ as in Apple. 'B' says /b/ as in Book. 'C' says /k/ as in Cat. Practice saying the sound as you point to each letter.
text.st: Tlhaku e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe ka Senyesemane e na le lebitso le molumo. 'A' e lla joalo ka ho Apple. 'B' e lla joalo ka ho Book. 'C' e lla joalo ka ho Cat.

text.en: Write big letters A, B, C on the chalkboard. Point to each letter and let all learners repeat the letter sound together three times.
text.st: Ngola litlhaku tse kholo A, B, C letlapeng. Supa tlhaku ka 'ngoe 'me baithuti bohle ba phete molumo oa tlhaku hammoho makhetlo a mararo.

q.en: Which word starts with the letter 'B'?
q.st: Ke lentsoe lefe le qalang ka tlhaku 'B'?

title.st: Mebala le Lintho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Name primary colours in English and identify coloured objects
outcome.st: Reha mebala ea mantlha ka Senyesemane le ho tseba lintho tsa teng

text.en: We see colours everywhere! The sky is blue. The grass on the hills is green. The ripe tomato is red. The bright sun is yellow.
text.st: Re bona mebala hohle! Leholimo le leputsoa (blue). Joang marallong bo botala (green). Tamati e butsoitseng e khubelu (red). Letsatsi le le mosehla (yellow).

text.en: Point to things in the classroom and ask: "What colour is this book?"
text.st: Supang lintho ka phaposing ’me le botse: "Ke 'mala ofe oo?"

q.en: What colour is fresh healthy summer grass on the mountains?
q.st: Ke 'mala ofe oa joang bo botala ba lithaba nakong ea lehlabula?

title.st: Ho Reka "Please" le "Thank You"

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Use courtesy words "please", "thank you", and "excuse me" naturally
outcome.st: Sebelisa mantsoe a tlhompho ka tlhaho

text.en: Good manners help us make friends. When you ask for something, say "Please". When someone gives you something, smile and say "Thank you".
text.st: Mekhoa e metle e re fa metsoalle. Ha u kopa ntho, re "Please" (Ke kopa). Ha motho a u fa ntho, bososela ebe u re "Thank you" (Kea leboha).

text.en: Practice handing a pen to a partner who responds with "Thank you!"
text.st: Koetlisang ho nehelana ka pene eo e mong a arabang ka "Thank you!"

q.en: What polite word should you say after your teacher gives you an exercise book?
q.st: Ke lentsoe lefe le nang le mekhoa e metle leo u lokelang ho le bua ha tichere e u fa buka?

title.st: Mantsoe a Liketso (Metsamao)

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Identify verbs that describe actions in daily life
outcome.st: Tseba mantsoe a hlalosang liketso bophelong ba letsatsi le letsatsi

text.en: A verb is an action word. It tells us what someone or something is doing. Examples of action words are: run, jump, sing, eat, read, and write.
text.st: Lentsoe la ketso le re bolella hore na motho kapa ntho e etsa eng. Mehlala ea mantsoe a liketso ke: matha (run), tlola (jump), bina (sing), ja (eat), bala (read), le ho ngola (write).

text.en: Call out an action word (e.g. 'jump', 'smile', 'sleep') and let learners act it out immediately.
text.st: Bitsa lentsoe la ketso (mohlala 'jump', 'smile', 'sleep') 'me u lumelle baithuti ho le etsa hang-hang.

q.en: Which of these words is an action word (verb)?
q.st: Ke lefe la mantsoe ana e leng lentsoe la ketso?

title.st: Mantsoe a Hananang

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Identify common pairs of opposites in English
outcome.st: Tseba lipara tsa mantsoe a hananang ka Senyesemane

text.en: Opposites are words with completely different meanings. Hot is opposite to cold. Big is opposite to small. Fast is opposite to slow. Up is opposite to down.
text.st: Mantsoe a hananang ke a nang le meelelo e sa tšoaneng ho hang. Hot (chesa) ke khahlanong le cold (bata). Big (kholo) ke khahlanong le small (nyane).

text.en: Play a Simon Says game using opposites: "Simon says look up! Simon says look down!"
text.st: Bapallang papali ea ho sheba holimo le tlase ka litaelo.

q.en: What is the opposite of the English word "tall"?
q.st: Lentsoe le hananang le "tall" (telele) ka Senyesemane ke lefe?

title.st: Ka Hare, Holimo, Tlas’a, le Kamorao

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Use prepositions to describe the exact position of objects
outcome.st: Sebelisa mantsoe a boemo ho hlalosa moo lintho li leng teng

text.en: Prepositions show where an object is located. The book is ON the table. The pen is IN the pencil case. The cat is sleeping UNDER the chair. The boy is hiding BEHIND the tree.
text.st: Litšupiso tsa libaka li bontša moo ntho e leng teng: Buka e HOLIMO (ON) tafoleng. Pene e KA HARE (IN) ho kesi. Katse e robetse TLAS’A (UNDER) setulo. Moshanyana o ipatile KAMORAO (BEHIND) ho sefate.

text.en: Place an eraser under a book and ask learners to describe where it is using a full sentence.
text.st: Behang raba tlas’a buka le botse baithuti ho hlalosa moo e leng teng ka polelo e feletseng.

q.en: The football rolled beneath the wooden bench. Which preposition describes its location?
q.st: Bolo e pitiketse tlas'a benche ea mapolanka. Ke lentsoe lefe le nepahetseng?

title.st: Mantsoe a ho umana (mareho)

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Understand core concepts of Naming words (nouns)
outcome.st: Utloisisa lintlha tsa sehlooho tsa thuto ena

text.en: A noun is a naming word. It names a person, a place or a thing. Teacher, school and book are nouns.
text.st: Lereho ke lentsoe le reng motho, sebaka kapa ntho. Titjhere, sekolo le buka ke mareho.

text.en: Ask learners to point to nouns in the classroom: desk, door, window.
text.st: Kopa bana ho supa mareho ka phaposing: tafole, monyako, fensetere.

q.en: Which word is a noun?
q.st: Ke lentsoe lefe e leng lereho?

title.st: Lipolelo Tse Bonolo: Moetsi le Ketso

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Construct simple sentences with a clear subject and predicate verb
outcome.st: Haha lipolelo tse bonolo tse nang le moetsi le leetsi le hlakileng

text.en: Every complete sentence tells a complete idea. It needs a subject (who or what does the action) and a verb (the action). Example: "The horse (subject) runs (verb) across the field."
text.st: Polelo efe kapa efe e nepahetseng e hlalosa mohopolo o feletseng. E hloka moetsi (subject) le ketso (verb). Mohlala: "The horse (pere) runs (ea matha) across the field."

text.en: Have learners underline the naming word and circle the doing word in sentences on the board.
text.st: Kopang baithuti ho thala tlas’a lebitso le ho etsa selika-likoe leetsing letlapeng.

q.en: In the sentence "The bird sings sweetly in the morning", what is the main action verb?
q.st: Polelong e reng "The bird sings sweetly in the morning", leetsi la ketso ke lefe?

title.st: Matšoao a Lipotso le a Makalo

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Use question marks and exclamation marks accurately in written English
outcome.st: Sebelisa letšoao la potso (?) le la makalo (!) ka nepo

text.en: When asking for information, we end our sentence with a Question Mark (?). Example: "Where is the clinic?" When expressing strong emotion or excitement, we use an Exclamation Mark (!). Example: "Watch out for the snake!"
text.st: Ha re botsa potso, re qetella ka Letšoao la Potso (?). Mohlala: "Where is the clinic?" Ha re bontša makalo kapa thabo e kholo, re sebelisa Letšoao la Makalo (!). Mohlala: "Watch out for the snake!"

text.en: Read sentences aloud changing your voice pitch so learners hear the musical difference.
text.st: Balang lipolelo ka lentsoe le phahameng le feto-fetohang ho bontša phapang ea melumo.

q.en: Which punctuation mark belongs at the end of the sentence: "How old are you"
q.st: Ke letšoao lefe la puo le loketseng qetellong ea polelo ena: "How old are you"

title.st: Litlhaku tse Kholo le Mathoko

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Use capital letters at sentence starts and names, and full stops at sentence ends
outcome.st: Sebelisa litlhaku tse kholo qalong ea polelo le mabitso, le matheba qetellong

text.en: Every complete sentence must start with a capital letter and end with a punctuation mark, like a full stop (.) or a question mark (?). Names of people and places always start with a capital letter, even in the middle of a sentence (e.g., 'Keketso visited Maseru.').
text.st: Polelo e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe e tlameha ho qala ka tlhaku e kholo 'me e fele ka letšoao, le kang letheba (.) kapa letšoao la potso (?). Mabitso a batho le libaka a qala ka tlhaku e kholo kamehla (mohlala, 'Keketso visited Maseru.').

text.en: Write an unpunctuated sentence on the chalkboard: 'we live in lesotho' and invite a learner to fix the capital letters and the full stop.
text.st: Ngola polelo e se nang matšoao letlapeng: 'we live in lesotho' 'me u meme moithuti ho lokisa litlhaku tse kholo le letheba.

q.en: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
q.st: Ke polelo efe e nang le matšoao a nepahetseng?
