title.en: Personal Pronouns: He, She, It, They, We
title.st: Liikemeli: He, She, It, They, We

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Replace repeated nouns with correct subject pronouns
outcome.st: Nka sebaka sa mabitso a phetoang ka liikemeli tse nepahetseng

text.en: Pronouns take the place of nouns so we do not repeat names again and again. Instead of "Thabo has a ball and Thabo kicks the ball", we say: "Thabo has a ball and HE kicks it." We use He for boys, She for girls, It for things, and They for groups.
text.st: Liikemeli li nka sebaka sa mabitso ho qoba ho pheta mabitso hape le hape. Ho e-na le ho re "Thabo o na le bolo ebe Thabo o e raha", re re: "Thabo has a ball and HE kicks it." He ke ea bashanyana, She ea banana, It ea lintho, They ea batho ba bangata.

text.en: Provide short paragraphs and challenge learners to count how many awkward repetitions are eliminated by pronouns.
text.st: Fanang ka serapa se nang le mabitso a phetiloeng baithuti ba a nkele sebaka ka liikemeli.

q.en: Choose the correct pronoun: "Mpho is a clever girl. ______ loves reading English stories."
q.st: Khetha seikemeli se nepahetseng: "Mpho is a clever girl. ______ loves reading English stories."

title.en: Finding the Main Idea in a Short Story
title.st: Ho Fumana Mohopolo oa Sehlooho Paleng

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Identify the central theme and supporting details in a descriptive passage
outcome.st: Tseba sehlooho se seholo le lintlha tse tšehetsang temaneng e khutšoanyane

text.en: The main idea is what a story or paragraph is mostly about. To find it, ask yourself: "Who or what is this whole text describing?" The supporting sentences give examples, reasons, or details that prove the main idea.
text.st: Mohopolo oa sehlooho ke ntho eo temana e buang ka eona haholo. E le hore u o fumane, ipotse: "Mongoli o bua ka eng haholo temaneng ee?" Lipolelo tse ling li tšehetsa le ho hlakisa mohopolo oo oa bohlokoa.

text.en: Teach learners to look closely at the very first and last sentence of a paragraph for clues.
text.st: Rutang baithuti ho shebisisa polelo ea pele le ea ho qetela temaneng bakeng sa malebela.

q.en: A passage describes cows grazing, sheep providing wool, and herdboys protecting them. What is the main idea?
q.st: Temana e hlalosa likhomo li fula, linku li fana ka boea, le balisana ba li lisa. Mohopolo oa sehlooho ke ofe?

options.en: Life and livestock herding in rural Lesotho
options.st: Bophelo ba leruo le balisana mahaeng a Lesotho

title.st: Mabitso a Khethehileng le a Tloaelehileng

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 English Syllabus p. 30, Outcome 17 (TG)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Senyesemane Sehlopha sa 5 p. 30, Sepheo 17 (TG)

outcome.en: read and use words with silent letters properly.
outcome.st: Bala le ho sebelisa mantsoe a nang le litlhaku tse sa bitsoeng hantle.

text.en: A noun is a word that names a person, place, thing, or animal. There are two main types: common nouns and proper nouns. A common noun names any person, place, or thing in general — for example, 'girl', 'city', or 'river'. A proper noun names a specific person, place, or thing and always starts with a capital letter — for example, 'Thabo', 'Maseru', or 'Caledon River'.
text.st: Lebitso ke lentsoe le bitsang motho, sebaka, ntho kapa pholo. Mefuta e 'meli ea bohlokoa ke mabitso a tloaelehileng le a khethehileng. Lebitso la tloaelehang le bitsa motho, sebaka kapa ntho ka kakaretso — mohlala, 'ngoanana', 'motse-moholo', kapa 'noka'. Lebitso la khethehileng le bitsa motho, sebaka kapa ntho e itseng 'me le qala ka tlhaku e kgolo — mohlala, 'Thabo', 'Maseru', kapa 'Noka ea Mohokare'.

text.en: Look at how proper and common nouns work in sentences: 'The girl walked to the market.' — 'girl' and 'market' are common nouns. 'Lineo walked to Maseru market.' — 'Lineo' and 'Maseru' are proper nouns. Notice that proper nouns always have a capital letter, wherever they appear in a sentence.
text.st: Sheba hore na mabitso a khethehileng le a tloaelehileng a sebetsa joang mafokong: 'Ngoanana o ile a tsamaea ho ea 'maraka.' — 'ngoanana' le ''maraka' ke mabitso a tloaelehileng. 'Lineo o ile a tsamaea ho ea 'maraka oa Maseru.' — 'Lineo' le 'Maseru' ke mabitso a khethehileng. Hlokomela hore mabitso a khethehileng a hloahloa ka tlhaku e kgolo, le ha a le hokae mafokong.

text.en: Write the headings 'Common Nouns' and 'Proper Nouns' on the board. Ask learners to look around the classroom and name five things they see. Write each name under the correct heading. Then help learners turn each word into a full sentence.
text.st: Ngola lihlooho 'Mabitso a Tloaelehileng' le 'Mabitso a Khethehileng' bortheng. Kopa barutuoa ba shebe kahara phaposi ea ho rutoa ba bitsa lintho tse hlano tseo ba li bonang. Ngola lebitso le leng le le leng tlasa hlooho e nepahetseng. Ebe o thuse barutuoa ho fetola lentsoe le leng le le leng mafokong a phethehileng.

q.en: Which sentence uses a proper noun correctly?
q.st: Ke molaetsa ofe o sebetsang lebitso la khethehileng ka nepo?

options.en: My friend lives in a City called maseru.
options.st: Motsoalle oa ka o phelang toropong e bitsoang maseru.

options.en: My friend Palesa lives in Maseru.
options.st: Motsoalle oa ka Palesa o phela Maseru.

options.en: My friend palesa lives in the city.
options.st: Motsoalle oa ka palesa o phela toropong.

title.en: Words with Silent Letters (Knee, Knife, Doubt, Climb)
title.st: Mantsoe a nang le Litlhaku Tse sa Buisoeng

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 5 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 5 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Read, spell, and pronounce words with silent letters accurately in spoken and written sentences
outcome.st: Bala, peleta le ho bitsa mantsoe a nang le litlhaku tse sa buisoeng ka nepo

text.en: In English, some words contain letters that are written but not pronounced aloud. Examples include silent "k" in *knife*, *knee*, and *know*; silent "b" in *climb*, *comb*, and *doubt*; and silent "w" in *write* and *wrist*. Recognizing these prevents spelling mistakes.
text.st: Senyesemaneng, mantsoe a mang a na le litlhaku tse ngoloang empa li sa bitsoe ka lentsoe. Mohlala: tlhaku ea "k" e khutsitseng mantsoeng a kang *knife* (thipa), *knee* (lengole), le *knock* (kokota); kapa "b" e khutsitseng ho *climb* (hloa) le *comb* (kama).

text.en: Have learners draw a "shushing finger" over silent letters in their exercise books to cement visual memory.
text.st: Etsang hore baithuti ba thale mola o bobebe tlas'a tlhaku e sa bitsoeng ha ba ngola mantsoe ao.

q.en: In the English word "KNIGHT" (a brave historical warrior), which two letters are silent when pronounced?
q.st: Lentsweng la Senyesemane le reng "KNIGHT", ke litlhaku life tse peli tse sa bitsoeng ha le buuoa?
q.sn: "K" qalong le "gh" bohareng lia khutsa; le bitsoa hantle joaloka "nite".

title.st: Mabitso a Kopantsoeng

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 English Syllabus p. 30, Outcome 10 (TG)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Senyesemane Sehlopha sa 5 p. 30, Sepheo 10 (TG)

outcome.en: construct sentences using compound nouns.
outcome.st: Aha lipolelo u sebelisa mareho-’moka (compound nouns).

text.en: A compound noun is a noun made by joining two or more words together to create a new meaning. Compound nouns can be written as one word, two separate words, or with a hyphen between them. For example: 'football' (one word), 'bus stop' (two words), and 'check-in' (hyphen). The new word has its own meaning that is different from each word on its own.
text.st: Lebitso la kopantsoeng ke lebitso le entsoe ka ho kopanya mantsoe a mabeli kapa a fetang ho theha moelelo o mocha. Mabitso a kopantsoeng a kgona ho ngoloa e le lentsoe le le leng, mantsoe a mabeli a arohaneng, kapa ka sophane pakeng tsa ona. Mohlala: 'football' (lentsoe le le leng), 'bus stop' (mantsoe a mabeli), le 'check-in' (sophane). Lentsoe le lecha le na le moelelo oa lona o fapaneng le oa lentsoe le leng le le leng ka bo lona.

text.en: Write the words 'sun', 'rain', 'book', 'fire', 'foot' on the board. Ask learners to find a second word to join each one and make a compound noun. Let them share their answers aloud and use each compound noun in a sentence.
text.st: Ngola mantsoe 'sun', 'rain', 'book', 'fire', 'foot' bortheng. Kopa barutuoa ba fumane lentsoe la bobeli la ho kopanya le le leng le le leng ho theha lebitso la kopantsoeng. Ba lumelle ho arolelana likarabo tsa bona ka molomo 'me ba sebetse lebitso le leng le le leng la kopantsoeng mafokong.

q.en: Which of the following is a compound noun?
q.st: Ke lefe la mantsoe a latelang lebitso la kopantsoeng?

title.st: Mabitso a Mong le a Bongata

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 English Syllabus p. 30, Outcome 11
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Senyesemane Sehlopha sa 5 p. 30, Sepheo 11

outcome.en: construct sentences using singular and plural forms of nouns.
outcome.st: Aha lipolelo u sebelisa mareho a bonngoe le bongata.

text.en: A singular noun names one person, place, or thing — for example, 'book', 'child', 'church'. A plural noun names more than one — for example, 'books', 'children', 'churches'. Most nouns become plural by adding '-s' or '-es'. Some nouns have irregular plural forms that you must remember, such as 'child → children', 'man → men', 'tooth → teeth', and 'mouse → mice'.
text.st: Lebitso la mong le bitsa motho a le mong, sebaka se se seng, kapa ntho e le nngoe — mohlala, 'buka', 'ngoane', 'kereke'. Lebitso la bongata le bitsa ho feta e le nngoe — mohlala, 'libuka', 'bana', 'likereke'. Mabitso a mangata a fetoha bongata ka ho eketsa '-s' kapa '-es'. Mabitso a mang a na le mefuta ea bongata e sa tloaelehang eo u tlamehang ho e hopola, joalo ka 'child → children', 'man → men', 'tooth → teeth', le 'mouse → mice'.

text.en: Make a matching game: write singular nouns on one set of cards and their plurals on another. Shuffle both sets and ask pairs of learners to match each singular to its correct plural. Discuss irregular plurals as a class.
text.st: Etsa papali ea ho bapisa: ngola mabitso a mong likareteng tse ling 'me bongata ba tsona likareteng tse ling. Thaeha sete tsohle tse peli 'me kopa barutuoa ba kopaneng ba babeli-babeli ho bapisa lebitso le leng le le leng la mong le bongata ba lona bo nepahetseng. Buisanang ka mabitso a bongata a sa tloaelehang joalo ka sehlopha.

q.en: What is the correct plural form of the noun 'woman'?
q.st: Ke bongata bo nepahetseng ba lebitso 'woman' (mosali) bo fe?

title.st: Nako e Fetileng, ea Hona le Nako le ea Tlang

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 English Syllabus p. 30, Outcome 12
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Senyesemane Sehlopha sa 5 p. 30, Sepheo 12

outcome.en: use past, present and future tenses correctly in sentences.
outcome.st: Sebelisa linako tse fetileng, tsa joale le tse tlang ka nepo lipolelong.

text.en: A verb can change its form to show when an action happens. The present tense shows an action happening now — 'She reads a book.' The past tense shows an action that already happened — 'She read a book yesterday.' The future tense shows an action that will happen later — 'She will read a book tomorrow.' To form the past tense, most verbs add '-ed', but irregular verbs change completely, like 'go → went' and 'eat → ate'.
text.st: Lefokonyane le kgona ho fetola sebopeho sa lona ho bontša nako eo ketso e etsahalang ka eona. Nako ea hona joale e bontša ketso e etsahalang joale — 'O bala buka.' Nako e fetileng e bontša ketso e seng e etsahala — 'O ne a bala buka maobane.' Nako ea tlang e bontša ketso e tla etsahala hamurao — 'O tla bala buka hosane.' Ho bopa nako e fetileng, mafokonyane a mangata a eketsa '-ed', empa mafokonyane a sa tloaelehang a fetola sebopeho sa ona kaofela, joalo ka 'go → went' le 'eat → ate'.

text.en: Draw a simple timeline on the board with 'Yesterday', 'Today', and 'Tomorrow' as markers. Say a verb aloud (e.g. 'walk') and ask learners to write sentences placing the action at each point on the timeline. Share and correct together.
text.st: Thaka mola o bonolo oa nako bortheng o nang le 'Maobane', 'Kajeno', le 'Hosane' joalo ka lipontso. Bolela lefokonyane ka molomo (mohlala 'walk') 'me kopa barutuoa ba ngole mafoko a behehang ketso sebakeng se seng le se seng molaong oa nako. Arolana 'me u batle se nepahetseng sehlopha.

q.en: Which sentence is written in the future tense?
q.st: Ke molaetsa ofe o ngotsoeng ka nako ea tlang?

options.en: The boys played football after school.
options.st: Bahlankana ba ile ba bapala bolo ka mora sekolo.

options.en: The boys are playing football now.
The boys will play football tomorrow.
options.st: Bahlankana ba tla bapala bolo hosane.

title.st: Lisupi tsa Ho Bapisa le tsa Ho Feta Tsohle

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 English Syllabus p. 30, Outcome 13
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Senyesemane Sehlopha sa 5 p. 30, Sepheo 13

outcome.en: use comparative and superlative forms of adjectives to describe things they see, smell, taste or touch.
outcome.st: Sebelisa comparative le superlative ea mahlaodi ho hlalosa lintho tseo ba li bonang, li fofonelang, latsoang kapa ba li amang.

text.en: An adjective describes a noun. When we compare two things, we use the comparative form of the adjective — we usually add '-er' to the end. For example: 'tall → taller'. When we compare three or more things and show which one has the most of a quality, we use the superlative form — we add '-est'. For example: 'tall → tallest'. For longer adjectives, we use 'more' for comparative and 'most' for superlative — 'beautiful → more beautiful → most beautiful'.
text.st: Supi e hlalosa lebitso. Ha re bapisa lintho tse peli, re sebetsa sebopeho sa ho bapisa sa supi — ka tloaelo re eketsa '-er' qetellong. Mohlala: 'tall → taller' (motelele → motelele haholoanyane). Ha re bapisa lintho tse tharo kapa ho feta 'me re bontša hore na e fe e nang le boleng bo bongata ka ho fetisisa, re sebetsa sebopeho sa ho feta tsohle — re eketsa '-est'. Mohlala: 'tall → tallest'. Lisupi tse telele, re sebetsa 'more' bakeng sa ho bapisa le 'most' bakeng sa ho feta tsohle — 'beautiful → more beautiful → most beautiful'.

text.en: Bring three objects of different sizes to class (e.g. a small stone, a medium stone, a large stone). Ask learners to describe them using the adjective 'big': 'big', 'bigger', 'biggest'. Then try with 'heavy' and 'light' to practise irregular and regular forms.
text.st: Tlisa lintho tse tharo tsa boholo bo fapaneng phapusing (mohlala, lejoe le lenyenyane, le bohareng, le le leholo). Kopa barutuoa ba li hlalose ka supi 'big': 'big', 'bigger', 'biggest'. Ebe u leke ka 'heavy' le 'light' ho itloaetsa mefuta e sa tloaelehang le e tloaelehang.

q.en: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: 'Mount Qiloane is ___ than the hill near our school.'
q.st: Khetha lentsoe le nepahetseng ho phethela molaetsa: 'Thaba ea Qiloane e ___ ho feta thaba e haufi le sekolo sa rona.'

title.en: Adverbs of Time, Manner and Place
title.st: Lisupi tsa Lefokonyane tsa Nako, Mokoa le Sebaka

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 English Syllabus p. 31, Outcome 21
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Senyesemane Sehlopha sa 5 p. 31, Sepheo 21

outcome.en: use adverbs of time, manner and place in sentences.
outcome.st: Sebelisa lithusi tsa maetsi tsa nako, mokhoa le sebaka lipolelong.

text.en: An adverb is a word that gives more information about a verb, an adjective, or another adverb. Adverbs of time tell us when something happens — for example, 'yesterday', 'now', 'soon', 'always'. Adverbs of manner tell us how something happens — for example, 'quickly', 'carefully', 'loudly'. Adverbs of place tell us where something happens — for example, 'here', 'outside', 'nearby', 'everywhere'.
text.st: Supi ea lefokonyane ke lentsoe le fang tlhahisoleseling e eketsehileng ka lefokonyane, supi kapa supi e 'ngoe ea lefokonyane. Lisupi tsa lefokonyane tsa nako li re bolella nako eo ntho e etsahalang ka eona — mohlala, 'maobane', 'joale', 'haufinyane', 'kamehla'. Lisupi tsa lefokonyane tsa mokoa li re bolella hore na ntho e etsahala joang — mohlala, 'kapele-kele', 'ka hloko', 'ka lentsoe le phahameng'. Lisupi tsa lefokonyane tsa sebaka li re bolella moo ntho e etsahalang teng — mohlala, 'mona', 'kantle', 'haufi', 'hohle-hohle'.

text.en: Write a simple sentence on the board, such as 'The dog barked.' Give each learner a strip of paper with one adverb on it. Ask them to come up and add their adverb to the sentence, then read it aloud. Discuss as a class which type of adverb was added each time.
text.st: Ngola molaetsa o bonolo bortheng, joalo ka 'Ntja e ile ea loma.' Fa morutuoa e mong le e mong sereite sa pampiri se nang le supi ea lefokonyane e le nngoe ho sona. Kopa ba tlo eketsa supi ea bona ea lefokonyane mafokong, ebe ba e bale ka molomo. Buisanang ka sehlopha hore ke mofuta mang oa supi ea lefokonyane o neng o eketswa nako le nako.

q.en: In the sentence 'She sang beautifully at the concert last night', which word is an adverb of manner?
q.st: Mafokong 'She sang beautifully at the concert last night' (O ile a bina ka bokhabane kontserteng bosiu boo bo fetileng), ke lentsoe lefe supi ea lefokonyane ea mokoa?

options.st: last night (bosiu boo bo fetileng — nako)

title.st: Liphošoloha

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 English Syllabus p. 31, Outcome 25 (TG)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Senyesemane Sehlopha sa 5 p. 31, Sepheo 25 (TG)

outcome.en: construct sentences using similes correctly.
outcome.st: Aha lipolelo u sebelisa litšoantšo tsa papiso (similes) ka nepo.

text.en: A simile is a figure of speech that compares two different things using the words 'like' or 'as'. Similes make our writing more interesting and help the reader picture what we are describing. For example: 'The river runs like a snake through the valley.' or 'She is as brave as a lion.' When you use a simile, you are not saying something is exactly something else — you are saying it is similar in one way.
text.st: Phošoloha ke sebopeho sa puo se bapisant hintho tse fapaneng ka ho sebetsa mantsoe 'like' (joalo ka) kapa 'as' (joalo ka). Liphošoloha li etsa hore ho ngola ha rona ho be le maikutlo 'me li thusa mmadi ho bona seo re se hlalossang. Mohlala: 'Noka e matha joalo ka noha molapo-watering.' kapa 'O sebete joalo ka tau.' Ha o sebetsa phošoloha, ha u bue hore ntho ke ntho e 'ngoe feela — u bua hore li tšoana ka tsela e le ngoe.

text.en: Here are some common similes you should know: 'as fast as a cheetah', 'as cold as ice', 'as bright as the sun', 'runs like the wind'. You can also create your own similes when you write. Think of something you want to describe, then find an animal, object, or idea that shares the same quality.
text.st: Ke liphošoloha tse tloaelehileng tseo u tlamehang ho tseba: 'as fast as a cheetah' (o potlaka joalo ka lengau), 'as cold as ice' (e bata joalo ka leqhoa), 'as bright as the sun' (e phatsima joalo ka letsatsi), 'runs like the wind' (o matha joalo ka moea). U kgona hape ho theha liphošoloha tsa hau ha u ngola. Nahana ntho eo u batlang ho e hlalosa, 'me u fumane pholo, ntho kapa mohopolo o tšoanang le boleng bo bong bo le bong.

text.en: Ask each learner to think of a family member or friend and describe them using at least two similes. For example: 'My grandmother is as wise as an owl and her voice is as soft as a whisper.' Let volunteers share with the class.
text.st: Kopa morutuoa e mong le e mong ho nahana ka leloko la lelapa kapa motsoalle 'me a mo hlalose ka ho sebetsa liphošoloha tse peli bonyane. Mohlala: 'Nkhono oa ka o na le bohlale joalo ka mangope, 'me lentsoe la hae le bonolo joalo ka tlhaela.' Lumella baithuti ba rata ho arolelana le sehlopha.

q.en: Which of the following sentences contains a simile?
q.st: Ke molaetsa ofe o latelang o nang le phošoloha?

options.en: The old man walked slowly to his house.
options.st: Nkhono o ile a tsamaea butle hae.

options.en: Her smile was like sunshine on a cold day.
options.st: Tsheko ea hae e ne e le joalo ka lehlabula la letsatsi letsatsi le batang.

options.en: The dog is very loyal to its owner.
options.st: Ntja e tsepahala haholo ho mong oa eona.

title.st: Ho Ngola Phatlalatso

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 English Syllabus p. 31, Outcome 27
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Senyesemane Sehlopha sa 5 p. 31, Sepheo 27

outcome.en: write a composition of two to three paragraphs.
outcome.st: Ngola moqoqo oa lirapa tse peli ho isa ho tse tharo.

text.en: A composition is a piece of writing that shares ideas, tells a story, or explains something. A good composition has a clear structure with a beginning, a middle, and an end. The beginning (introduction) introduces the topic and grabs the reader's attention. The middle (body) gives the main ideas and details. The end (conclusion) wraps up your ideas and finishes the composition neatly.
text.st: Phatlalatso ke karolo ea ho ngola e arolelang mehopolo, e bolellang pale kapa e hlalosang ntho. Phatlalatso e ntle e na le sebopeho se hlakileng se nang le qalo, bohareng le qetelo. Qalo (selelekela) e hlahisa sehlooho 'me e hohela hloko ea mmadi. Bohareng (setopo) se fana ka mehopolo e meholo le lintlha. Qetelo e phutha mehopolo ea hau 'me e phethela phatlalatso ka toka.

text.en: When you write your composition, follow these steps: (1) Choose a topic you know well or find interesting. (2) Plan your ideas — write a few notes before you start. (3) Write your first paragraph to introduce the topic. (4) Write one or two body paragraphs with your main points. (5) Write a conclusion that sums up what you wrote. (6) Read your work and check for spelling, punctuation, and grammar mistakes.
text.st: Ha u ngola phatlalatso ea hau, latela mehato ena: (1) Khetha sehlooho seo u se tsebang hantle kapa seo u se fumanang se kgahlisang. (2) Retha mehopolo ea hau — ngola lintlha tse 'maloa pele o qala. (3) Ngola phetoho ea hau ea pele ho hlahisa sehlooho. (4) Ngola liphetoho tse nngoe tse peli tsa 'molapo' ka lintlha tsa hau tse kholo. (5) Ngola qetelo e phophometsang seo u se ngotseng. (6) Bala mosebetsi oa hau 'me u hlahlobe phoso tsa ho ngola, pontšo le grama.

text.en: Give learners a composition frame with three blank boxes labelled 'Introduction', 'Body', and 'Conclusion'. Ask them to write 2–3 sentences in each box about the topic 'My Favourite Day'. Walk around to give feedback before they write their full composition.
text.st: Fa barutuoa sebopeho sa phatlalatso se nang le lebokose le ka mong le selemo sa 'Selelekela', 'Setopo', le 'Qetelo'. Kopa ba ngole mafoko a 2–3 kareteng e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe mabapi le sehlooho 'Letsatsi la Ka le Ratehang Ka ho Fetisisa'. Tsamaea ho fa malebela pele ba ngola phatlalatso e phethehileng.

q.en: Which part of a composition introduces the topic and catches the reader's attention?
q.st: Ke karolo efe ea phatlalatso e hlahisang sehlooho 'me e hohela hloko ea mmadi?

title.en: Using a Dictionary Effectively: Alphabetical Order & Guide Words
title.st: Ho Sebelisa Dictionary ka Makhethe

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 English Syllabus p. 30, Outcome 6
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Senyesemane Sehlopha sa 5 p. 30, Sepheo 6

outcome.en: use a dictionary effectively.
outcome.st: Sebelisa bukana ea tlhaloso ea mantsoe (dictionary) ka mokhoa o atlehileng.

text.en: A dictionary arranges words in strict alphabetical order from A to Z. Guide words at the very top of each page show the first and last word on that page, saving you time. A dictionary entry tells you the word's spelling, pronunciation, part of speech (noun, verb, adjective), and exact definition.
text.st: Bukana ea mantsoe (dictionary) e hlophisa mantsoe ho latela tatellano ea alfabeta ho tloha ho A ho isa ho Z. Mantsoe a tataisang (guide words) a holimo leqepheng a u bontša lentsoe la pele le la ho qetela leqepheng leo. E u fa thlahiso ea mongolo, mofuta oa lentsoe, le moelelo oa lona o hlakileng.

text.en: Race game: Call out three random words (e.g., "Blanket", "Basotho", "Breeze") and challenge students to arrange them in strict dictionary order.
text.st: Bapallang lebelo la ho hlophisa mantsoe a mararo ho latela tlhaku ea pele, ea bobeli le ea boraro ea alfabeta.

q.en: Which of the following words appears FIRST in a standard English dictionary?
q.st: Ke lentsoe lefe har'a a latelang le tla hlaha PELE ka hare ho dictionary ea Senyesemane?
q.sn: Hobane kaofela a qala ka "C", re sheba tlhaku ea bobeli: "a" e tla pele ho "e" le "o" (Cattle -> Circle -> Cloud).

topic.st: Puo e Tobileng le e sa Tobileng

title.st: Ho Sebelisa Puo e Tobileng le e sa Tobileng

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Convert direct speech into reported/indirect speech
outcome.st: Fetola puo e tobileng ho ba puo e tlalehiloeng

text.en: Direct speech repeats the exact words a person spoke, enclosed inside quotation marks: Lineo said, "I am going home." Indirect (reported) speech explains what someone said without exact quotes: Lineo said that she was going home. Notice the change in tense and pronoun.
text.st: Puo e tobileng e pheta mantsoe a nnete ao motho a a buileng, a kentsoeng ka har'a li-quotation marks: Lineo said, "I am going home." Puo e sa tobileng e tlaleha seo motho a se buileng: Lineo said that she was going home.

text.en: Have Learner A whisper a sentence to Learner B. Learner B then tells the whole class in reported speech: 'She said that...'
text.st: Etsa hore Moithuti A a sebelise mantsoe ho Moithuti B. Moithuti B a be a bolelle phapusi eohle ka puo e tlalehiloeng: 'She said that...'

q.en: Which is the correct reported speech for: Mpho said, "I like reading"?
q.st: Ke efe e nepahetseng bakeng sa: Mpho said, "I like reading"?

options.en: Mpho said that she liked reading.
options.st: Mpho said that she liked reading.

options.en: Mpho says that I like reading.
options.st: Mpho says that I like reading.

title.en: Joining Sentences with Although, Because, and However
title.st: Ho Kopanya Lipolelo ka Although, Because, le However

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Combine complex ideas using cause and contrast conjunctions
outcome.st: Kopanya mehopolo e tebileng u sebelisa mahlakantsi a lebaka le phapang

text.en: Conjunctions connect independent ideas smoothly. We use "because" to show reasons ("We boiled water because it had germs"). We use "although" or "however" to show contrast ("Although it rained heavily, the football game continued").
text.st: Mahlakantsi a kopanya mehopolo e fapaneng ka makhethe. Re sebelisa "because" (hobane) ho fana ka lebaka. Re sebelisa "although" (leha) ho bontša ntho e etsahetseng ho sa tsotellehe tšitiso.

text.en: Give halves of sentences on cards and ask students to match cause with consequence.
text.st: Fanang ka likarete tsa halofo ea polelo ebe baithuti ba kopanya lebaka le sephetho.

q.en: Fill in the blank: "Mpho passed her final examinations ______ she studied diligently every evening."
q.st: Tlatsa sebaka: "Mpho passed her final examinations ______ she studied diligently every evening."

title.st: Ho Fetola Lipolelo ho Tloha ho Active ho Ea ho Passive

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Differentiate and convert sentences between active and passive voice
outcome.st: Khaohanya le ho fetola lipolelo pakeng tsa lentsoe le etsang le le etsoang

text.en: In the Active Voice, the subject performs the action: "The shepherd sheared the sheep." In the Passive Voice, the focus shifts to the receiver: "The sheep was sheared by the shepherd." We use passive voice when the result is more important than who did it.
text.st: Lentsweng le etsang (Active), moetsi o etsa ketso ka kotloloho: "The shepherd sheared the sheep." Lentsweng le etsoang (Passive), mahlo a sheba ntho e etsahetseng: "The sheep was sheared by the shepherd."

text.en: Show newspaper headlines where passive voice is commonly used (e.g., "Bridge Opened in Mohale's Hoek").
text.st: Bontšang lihlooho tsa likoranta moo passive voice e sebelisoang haholo.

q.en: Convert to passive voice: "The students planted twenty indigenous trees."
q.st: Fetolela ho passive voice: "The students planted twenty indigenous trees."

options.en: Twenty indigenous trees were planted by the students.
options.st: Twenty indigenous trees were planted by the students.

options.en: The students are planting trees tomorrow.
options.st: The students are planting trees tomorrow.

title.st: Ho Haha Mabaka Phehisanong

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Present clear evidence and counter-arguments in formal debates
outcome.st: Fana ka bopaki bo hlakileng le mabaka a utloahalang phehisanong

text.en: In a formal debate, two teams argue for and against a motion (e.g. 'School uniforms should be compulsory'). A strong debater always states their point, gives supporting evidence or real-life examples, and refutes the opposing team's arguments politely and respectfully.
text.st: Phehisanong ea semmuso, lihlopha tse peli li phehisana ka taba. Moithuti ea hloahloa o hlahisa ntlha ea hae, o fana ka bopaki le mehlala ea sebele, 'me o araba khanyetso ea sehlopha se seng ka mekhoa e nang le tlhompho le bohlale.

text.en: Organize a 10-minute classroom debate on: 'Students should not have homework on weekends'. Split learners into Proposition and Opposition.
text.st: Hlophisa phehisano ea metsotso e 10 ka: 'Baithuti ha ba lokela ho fuoa mosebetsi oa hae mafelong a beke'. Arola baithuti ka mahlakore a mabeli.

q.en: What makes an argument persuasive and effective in a debate?
q.st: Ke eng se etsang hore lebaka le be le matla le ho kholisa phehisanong?

options.en: Clear logic, factual evidence, and calm delivery
options.st: Mabaka a utloahalang, bopaki, le ho bua ka khotso

options.en: Shouting louder than the other speakers
options.st: Ho hooa ka matla ho feta ba bang
Ho kgaola batho hanong ha ba bua

title.en: Writing a Formal Application or Request Letter
title.st: Ho Ngola Lengolo la Kopo kapa la Semmuso

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Format and write a formal business letter with two addresses, date, and formal salutation
outcome.st: Hlophisa le ho ngola lengolo la semmuso le nang le liaterese tse peli le teboho ea tlhompho

text.en: A formal letter is used for business, government officials, or school principals. It features two addresses (sender top right, recipient top left), date, formal salutation ("Dear Sir/Madam"), clear subject line, polite body, and sign-off ("Yours sincerely").
text.st: Lengolo la semmuso le ngoloa ho baokameli kapa lihlooho tsa likolo. Le na le liaterese tse peli (ea hao holimo ka letsohong le letona, ea moamoheli ka le letšehali), letsatsi, tumeliso ea semmuso, le qetello e reng "Yours faithfully / sincerely".

text.en: Have learners draft a formal letter requesting permission to use the community hall for an ICT exhibition.
text.st: Etsang hore baithuti ba ngole lengolo la kopo ea holo ea motse bakeng sa pontšo ea ICT.

q.en: What is the correct complementary closing when writing a formal letter to an unknown recipient addressed as "Dear Sir/Madam"?
q.st: Ke teboho efe e nepahetseng ea ho qetela lengolong la semmuso le lebisitsoeng ho "Dear Sir/Madam"?

topic.st: Ho Bala ka Bohlale le Tlhahlobo

title.st: Ho Khetholla Nnete ho Maikutlo

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (English)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Linguistic & Literary (Senyesemane)

outcome.en: Distinguish objective verifiable facts from personal subjective opinions in texts
outcome.st: Khaohanya nnete e tiileng ho maikutlo a motho a inahaneloang

text.en: A Fact is a statement that can be proven true with evidence or measurement (e.g., "Maseru is the capital city of Lesotho"). An Opinion is a personal belief or feeling that cannot be proven true or false (e.g., "Maths is the most wonderful subject in the world").
text.st: Nnete (Fact) ke taba e nang le bopaki bo ka netefatsoang (mohlala: "Maseru ke motse-moholo oa Lesotho"). Maikutlo (Opinion) ke maikutlo kapa tšepo ea motho e ke keng ea netefatsoa e le molao (mohlala: "Lipalo ke thuto e monate ka ho fetisisa lefatšeng").

text.en: Bring newspaper advertisements and ask learners to circle opinion words like "best", "delicious", "amazing".
text.st: Tlisang lipapatso tsa likoranta le ba kope ho thala tlas'a mantsoe a maikutlo a kang "e ntle ka ho fetisisa".

q.en: Which of the following sentences represents an objective, verifiable fact?
q.st: Ke polelo efe har'a tse latelang e emelang nnete e tiileng e ka pakwang ka bopaki?

options.en: The Katse Dam wall is located in the Kingdom of Lesotho.
options.st: Letamo la Katse le fumaneha ka hare ho ’Muso oa Lesotho.

options.en: Winter snow in Lesotho is much prettier than autumn leaves.
options.st: Lehloa la mariha le letle ho feta mahlohonolo a hoetla.

options.en: All goats prefer yellow grass over green grass.
options.st: Lipoli tsohle li rata joang bo bosehla ho feta bo botala.

title.st: Litumeliso tsa Letsatsi le Letsatsi

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Greet elders and peers respectfully at different times of the day
outcome.st: Lumelisa ba baholo le lithaka ka tlhompho ka linako tse fapaneng tsa letsatsi

text.en: In Sesotho, greetings show kindness and respect. In the morning we say: 'Lumela ntate' or 'Lumela 'm'e'. When greeting many people together we say: 'Lumelang'.
text.st: Ka Sesotho, litumeliso li bonts'a botho le tlhompho. Hoseng re re: 'Lumela ntate' kapa 'Lumela 'm'e'. Ha re lumelisa batho ba bangata re re: 'Lumelang'.

text.en: Have learners practice pairing up and taking turns greeting each other politely with eye contact.
text.st: Lumella baithuti ho ikopanya ka bobeli 'me ba fapanyetsane ho lumelisana ka mekhoa e metle le tlhompho.

q.en: U lumelisa tichere ea hao ea monna joang hoseng ka Sesotho?
q.st: U lumelisa tichere ea hao ea monna joang hoseng ka Sesotho?

title.en: Melumo ea Litlhaku: A, E, I, O, U
title.st: Melumo ea Litlhaku: A, E, I, O, U

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Pronounce the five Sesotho vowels clearly and identify words starting with them
outcome.st: Bitsa lihlaku tse hlano tsa liluma-’moho ka nepo le ho fumana mantsoe a qalang ka tsona

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Sesotho has 5 core vowel sounds: a (joaloka apole), e (joaloka esele), i (joaloka intshi), o (joaloka oache), u (joaloka utloa). Melumo ena ke motheo oa ho bala Sesotho ka thello.
text.st: Sesotho se na le liluma-’moho tse hlano: A, E, I, O, U. A (apole), E (esele), I (intshi), O (oache), U (utloa). Melumo ena ke motheo oa ho bala Sesotho ka thello le ho ngola hantle.

text.en: Sing vowel rhymes with bodily gestures to anchor sound recognition.
text.st: Binang pina ea liluma-’moho le etsa metsamao ea matsoho ho tiisa tsebo ea melumo.

q.en: Lentsoe "esele" le qala ka tlhaku efe har'a liluma-’moho tsa Sesotho?
q.st: Lentsoe "esele" le qala ka tlhaku efe har'a liluma-’moho tsa Sesotho?

title.en: Mabitso a Likarolo tsa ’Mele oa Motho
title.st: Mabitso a Likarolo tsa ’Mele oa Motho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Identify and name body parts correctly in Sesotho
outcome.st: Tseba le ho reha likarolo tsa ’mele ka nepo ka Sesotho

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Re hloka ho tseba likarolo tsa ’mele ea rona: Hlooho (head), Mahlo a mabeli a ho bona (eyes), Litsebe tse peli tsa ho utloa (ears), Nko ea ho hema (nose), Molomo oa ho ja le ho bua (mouth), le Matsoho a ho sebetsa (hands).
text.st: Re hloka ho tseba likarolo tsa ’mele ea rona: Hlooho, Mahlo a mabeli a ho bona, Litsebe tse peli tsa ho utloa, Nko ea ho hema, Molomo oa ho bua le ho ja, le Matsoho a ho sebetsa le ho ngola.

text.en: Play "Tšoara nko! Tšoara litsebe!" where learners touch the part named.
text.st: Bapallang "Tšoara litsebe! Tšoara hlooho!" ho netefatsa kutloisiso ea mantsoe.

q.en: Re sebelisa karolo efe ea ’mele ho mamela lentsoe la tichere le melumo?
q.st: Re sebelisa karolo efe ea ’mele ho mamela lentsoe la tichere le melumo?

title.st: Lipina tsa Bana le Lithokoana

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Recite traditional rhymes and children's songs with rhythm
outcome.st: Pheta lithoko le lipina tsa setso ka morethetho

text.en: Basotho children have songs for playtime, for herding, and for bedtime stories. Clapping to the rhythm makes the language memorable and fun.
text.st: Bana ba Basotho ba na le lipina tsa lipapali, tsa boliche le tsa lipale. Ho opa liatla ho tsamaeang le morethetho ho etsa hore puo e hopolehe habonolo 'me e thabise.

text.en: Sing a popular children's rhyme like 'Mmankokotelo' together as a whole class while clapping.
text.st: Binang pina e tummeng ea bana hammoho phapusing eohle ha le ntse le opa liatla.

q.en: Ke eng se thusang bana ho ithuta le ho hopola mantsoe a Sesotho habonolo lipapaling?
q.st: Ke eng se thusang bana ho ithuta le ho hopola mantsoe a Sesotho habonolo lipapaling?

title.en: Mabitso a Bahlokomeli le Litho tsa Lelapa
title.st: Mabitso a Bahlokomeli le Litho tsa Lelapa

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Use traditional Sesotho kinship terms appropriately
outcome.st: Sebelisa mabitso a tšoanetseng a likamano tsa borapeli le lelapa

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Sesotho se na le tlotlontsoe e ruileng ea likamano tsa lelapa: Ntate ke tsoali ea monna, ’Mè ke tsoali ea mosali. Moena ke ngoana oa monyenyane, Moholoane ke ngoana oa moholo ho uena. Malome ke ngoanabo ’mè oa monna, Rakgadi ke kgaitsedi ea ntate.
text.st: Sesotho se na le tlotlontsoe e ntle haholo ea lelapa: Ntate le ’Mè ke batsoali. Moena ke ngoaneno e monyenyane ho uena, Moholoane ke e moholo. Malome ke kgaitsedi ea ’mè, ha Rakgadi e le kgaitsedi ea ntate.

text.en: Discuss how maternal and paternal aunts and uncles have distinct traditional responsibilities.
text.st: Hlalosang karolo ea bohlokoa ea Malome le Rakgadi litabeng tsa setso tsa lelapa.

q.en: Ka setso sa Sesotho, ngoanabo ’mè oa monna u mo bitsa mang?
q.st: Ka setso sa Sesotho, ngoanabo ’mè oa monna u mo bitsa mang?

title.en: Ho Bala Lintho ka Sesotho: Nngoe ho isa Leshomeng
title.st: Ho Bala Lintho ka Sesotho: Nngoe ho isa Leshomeng

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Count from one to ten fluently using formal Sesotho counting terminology
outcome.st: Bala ho tloha ho nngoe ho isa leshomeng ka mantsoe a nepahetseng a Sesotho

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Ha re bala linomoro ka Sesotho, re re: Nngoe (1), Peli (2), Tharo (3), ’Nè (4), Hlano (5), Tseletseng (6), Supileng (7), Robeli (8), Robong (9), Leshome (10). Linomoro tsena li ngoloa ka mantsoe lithutong tsa Sesotho.
text.st: Ha re bala linomoro ka Sesotho, re re: Nngoe (1), Peli (2), Tharo (3), ’Nè (4), Hlano (5), Tseletseng (6), Supileng (7), Robeli (8), Robong (9), Leshome (10). Ho bohlokoa ho tseba ho li ngola ka mongolo.

text.en: Practice counting cattle, sheep, or trees in the school vicinity using pure Sesotho words.
text.st: Balanang lintho tsa lebala (lifate, litafole) le sebelisa mantsoe a Sesotho a hloekileng.

q.en: Lentsoe la Sesotho le emelang palo ea "7" ke lefe?
q.st: Lentsoe la Sesotho le emelang palo ea "7" ke lefe?

title.st: Mmutla le Pula

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Understand core concepts of The Hare and the Rain
outcome.st: Utloisisa lintlha tsa sehlooho tsa thuto ena

text.en: Hare lived on a mountain. One day the rain came down hard. Hare found a big rock and hid under it. Then he called his friends: “Come under the rock!” Everyone stayed dry and happy. Sharing is good.
text.st: Mmutla o ne a ahile thabeng. Letsatsi le leng pula ea na haholo. Mmutla a fumana lefika le leholo ’me a ipata tlasa lona. Eaba o bitsa metsoalle ea hae: “Tlong tlasa lefika!” Bohle ba lula ba omme ba thabile. Ho arolelana ho molemo.

text.en: Read aloud, then ask learners to retell the story in their own words.
text.st: Bala ka lentsoe le phahameng, ebe u kopa bana ho pheta pale ka mantsoe a bona.

q.en: Where did Hare shelter from the rain?
q.st: Mmutla o ile a ipata pula kae?

title.st: Lilotho le Bohlale ba tsona

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Engage with Sesotho traditional riddles to sharpen quick thinking
outcome.st: Rarolla lilotho tsa Sesotho ho chorisa kelello le lebelo la mohopolo

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Lilotho ke papali ea bohlale e rutang bana ho nahanisisa le ho hlahloba lintho tsa tlhaho. Ha motho a qala selotho o re: "Ka n'e re ka re..." ebe ba bang ba re: "Rea o thutha!" Mohlala: "Ka n'e re ka re: Monnamoholo o teetsoe hare ke majoe?" Karabo ke: Leleme le menong.
text.st: Lilotho ke papali ea khale ea bohlale. Ha e qala motho o re: "Ka n'e re ka re..." ebe ba bang ba araba ka ho re: "Rea o thutha!" Mohlala: "Monnamoholo o teetsoe hare ke majoe?" Karabo ke: Leleme le pota-potiloe ke meno.

text.en: Invite learners to share riddles taught to them by grandparents at home.
text.st: Kopang baithuti ho arolelana lilotho tseo ba li rutiloeng ke bo-nkhono hae.

q.en: Selotho: "Ka n'e re ka re: Masimong ho letse nare e kholo e senang maoto?" Karabo ke eng?
q.st: Selotho: "Ka n'e re ka re: Masimong ho letse nare e kholo e senang maoto?" Karabo ke eng?

options.en: Mokopu kapa lerotse le letse fatše
options.st: Mokopu (lerotse) le leholo le letse masimong

title.en: Lithoko tsa Likhomo le Pere ea Sesotho
title.st: Lithoko tsa Likhomo le Pere ea Sesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Recite simple traditional praise poetry with appropriate rhythm and voice inflection
outcome.st: Pheta lithokoana tse khutšoanyane tsa setso ka morethetho o nepahetseng

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Lithoko ke bonono ba bohlokoa haholo moetlong oa Basotho. Re rorisa marena, bagale, le liphoofolo tsa rona: "Khomo molimo o nko e metsi, khomo e tsoang lefung la motho!" E bontša kamoo likhomo li ananeloang kateng bakeng sa lebese, temo le tebeletso.
text.st: Lithoko ke bonono bo phahameng ba puo ea Sesotho. Lithoko tsa likhomo li re: "Khomo molimo o nko e metsi, o pholosang batho lefung!" E bontša tlotla e kholo eo khomo e nang le eona sechabeng sa Basotho.

text.en: Demonstrate the traditional posture and powerful voice used when reciting thoko.
text.st: Bontšang boemo ba ’mele le lentsoe le tiileng le sebelisoang ha ho thokoa.

q.en: Hobaneng ha khomo e bitsoa "molimo o nko e metsi" thothokisong ea Sesotho?
q.st: Hobaneng ha khomo e bitsoa "molimo o nko e metsi" thothokisong ea Sesotho?

options.en: Hobane e fa batho bophelo ka lebese, nama, le temo
options.st: Hobane e fa batho bophelo ka lebese, nama, le temo

options.en: Hobane e lula ka hare ho linoka letsatsi lohle
Hobane e hloka ho nesoa ke pula feela

title.st: Morabaraba le Lipapali tsa Bohlale

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Describe the rules and strategic thinking behind the traditional game of Morabaraba
outcome.st: Hlalosa melao le bohlale ba papali ea setso ea Morabaraba

text.en: Morabaraba is a traditional ancient Basotho strategy board game played with 12 tokens ('cows' or likhomo) each on a board drawn in the dirt or on stone. Players must plan ahead, block their opponent, and form rows of three ('likhutsana') to capture tokens.
text.st: Morabaraba ke papali ea setso ea bohlale ea Basotho e bapaloang ka likhomo tse 12 ka lehlakore boardeng e thaliloeng mobung kapa lejoeng. Libapali li rala maano, ho thibela mohanyetsi, le ho etsa mothapo oa tse tharo ho thunya likhomo.

text.en: Draw a Morabaraba board on paper or chalkboard. Use bottle tops of two different colours to demonstrate a game opening.
text.st: Thala board ea Morabaraba pampiring kapa letlapeng. Sebelisa likhurumelo tsa mebala e 'meli e fapaneng ho bonts'a qalo ea papali.

q.en: Libapali tsa Morabaraba li qala ka likhomo tse kae ka lehlakore le leng le le leng?
q.st: Libapali tsa Morabaraba li qala ka likhomo tse kae ka lehlakore le leng le le leng?

title.en: Maele a Bontšang Tšebelisano le Bonngoe
title.st: Maele a Bontšang Tšebelisano le Bonngoe

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Interpret proverbs emphasizing teamwork and community solidarity in daily life
outcome.st: Hlalosa maele a khothalletsang tšebelisano-’moho le bonngoe sechabeng

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Maele a Sesotho a na le bohlale bo tebileng bo siiloeng ke baholo-holo ba rona. Maele a reng: "Kopano ke matla" le "Matsoho a hlatsoana" a re ruta hore ha re sebetsa ’moho re le sechaba, re ka hlola mathata afe kapa afe, joaloka mekolokotlane ea matsema.
text.st: Maele a Sesotho a re ruta bohlale ba bophelo. Maele a reng: "Kopano ke matla" le "Letsogo le leng ha le hlatsoe le leng" a bontša hore tšebelisano le thusano ke tsona tse ahang motse le sechaba se phetseng hantle.

text.en: Ask learners how their parents practice "letsema" when weeding fields or harvesting.
text.st: Botsang baithuti hore na batsoali ba bona ba sebelisa "letsema" joang masimong.

q.en: Maele a reng "Kopano ke matla" a ruta eng?
q.st: Maele a reng "Kopano ke matla" a ruta eng?

options.en: Hore batho ba fihlella katleho e kholo ha ba sebetsa ’moho
options.st: Hore batho ba fihlella katleho e kholo ha ba sebetsa ’moho

options.en: Hore motho e mong le e mong a iketsetse a le mong

title.en: Tšebeliso ea Koma le Khutlo Polelong
title.st: Tšebeliso ea Koma le Khutlo Polelong

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Apply commas and full stops accurately in Sesotho sentence construction
outcome.st: Sebelisa khutlo (.) le koma (,) ka nepo ha u ngola lipolelo tsa Sesotho

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Ha re ngola Sesotho, re sebelisa Khutlo (.) qetellong ea polelo e hlalosang taba. Re sebelisa Koma (,) ho phomola hanyenyane ha re bala le ha re thathamisa lintho: "Masimong re leme poone, mabele, linaoa, le meroho."
text.st: Khutlo (.) e emela pheletso ea mohopolo polelong. Koma (,) e sebelisoa ha ho thathamisoa lintho kapa ho bontša phomolo e khutšoanyane: "Mamasianoke o ile a reka liapole, liperekisi, le libanana lebenkeleng."

text.en: Have learners read aloud taking a soft breath at every comma and a full stop pause at every khutlo.
text.st: Etsang hore baithuti ba phomole hanyenyane komeng le ho ema ka ho feletseng khutlong ha ba bala.

q.en: Re lokela ho beha letšoao lefe qetellong ea polelo ena: "Morena Moshoeshoe I o ne a rata khotso"
q.st: Re lokela ho beha letšoao lefe qetellong ea polelo ena: "Morena Moshoeshoe I o ne a rata khotso"

title.st: Bua ka Boitsepo ka Taba

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Sesotho Syllabus p. 1, Outcome 1 (TG)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Sesotho Sehlopha sa 5 p. 1, Sepheo 1 (TG)

outcome.en: Speak confidently about an unprepared topic (bua ka boitšepo ka taba eo ba sa itokisetsang eona.)
outcome.st: bua ka boitšepo ka taba eo ba sa itokisetsang eona.

text.en: When you speak about a topic in front of other learners, it is important to prepare. Start by thinking about what you will say, then speak in clear words. Look at other people when you speak, and do not be afraid. Confidence comes with practice.
text.st: Ha o bua ka taba pele ha baithuti ba bang, ho bohlokoa ho itokisetsa. Qala ka ho nahana ka seo o tla se bua, ebe o bua ka mantsoe a hlaka. Lebelela batho ba bang ha o bua, 'me u se ke ua tšaba. Boitsepo bo tla tla ha o itaetsa.

text.en: Learners in Lesotho learn to speak about many different topics — such as farming, animals, cultural images, and traditions. Use your knowledge of everyday life when you speak.
text.st: Baithuti ba Lesotho ba ithuta ho bua ka taba tse fapaneng — joalo ka temo, mapolasi, litšoantšo tsa setso, le litumelo. Sebelisa tsebo ea hao ea bophelo ba letsatsi le letsatsi ha o bua.

text.en: Give the learner five minutes to prepare, then ask them to speak about something they enjoy doing as a chore — such as cooking, talking with their father, or herding cattle. Other learners listen and ask one question.
text.st: Fa moithuti nako ea metsotso e mehlano ho itokisetsa, ebe o mo kopa ho bua ka ntho eo a e ratang ho e etsa ka mpho — joalo ka ho jalloa, ho bua le ba ntatae, kapa ho reala likhomo. Baithuti ba bang ba mamele ebe ba botsa potso e le ngoe.

q.en: What helps a learner speak confidently in front of other learners?
q.st: Ke eng se thusang moithuti ho bua ka boitsepo pele ha baithuti ba bang?

options.st: Ho bua kapele-pele ntle le ho nahana

options.en: Preparing and looking at people while speaking
options.st: Ho itokisetsa 'me o lebelele batho ha o bua

options.en: Speaking quietly so others cannot hear
options.st: Ho bua koung, hore ba bang ba se ke ba utloa

title.st: Bala Buka ea Pale ka Kutloisiso

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Sesotho Syllabus p. 1, Outcome 4
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Sesotho Sehlopha sa 5 p. 1, Sepheo 4

outcome.en: Read a story book with comprehension (bala buka ea pale ka kutloisiso.)
outcome.st: bala buka ea pale ka kutloisiso.

text.en: When you read a story, do not just read the words. Think about what is happening in the story. Ask yourself: 'Who is speaking? What is happening? Where is it happening?' These questions will help you understand the story better.
text.st: Ha o bala pale, o se ke oa bala feela mantsoe. Nahana ka seo se etsahalang polelong. Botsa boitspreng: 'Ke mang ea bualang? Ke eng se etsahalang? Ho etsahala kae?' Lipotso tsena li tla o thusa ho utloisisa pale hamolemo.

text.en: Sesotho stories often carry important messages — such as respecting elders, helping one another, and living in peace. As you read, pay attention to the message of the story, not just the words.
text.st: Dipale tsa Sesotho hangata di na le melaetsa ea bohlokoa — joalo ka ho hlompha ba baholo, ho thusana, le ho phela ka kagiso. Ha o bala, hlokomela molaetsa oa pale eseng feela mantsoe.

text.en: Read a short story in Sesotho with Basotho cultural content — such as the story of 'Mmuso and his Cow'. After reading, ask learners to answer three questions: Who is the main character? What happened? What does this story teach us?
text.st: Bala pale e khutshoane ka puo ea Sesotho e nang le setso sa Basotho — joalo ka pale ea 'Mmuso le Khomo ea hae'. Kamora ho bala, kopa baithuti ho araba lipotso tse tharo: Ke mang sehlooho sa pale? Ke eng se etsahalileng? Pale ena e re ruta eng?

q.en: What helps a learner understand a story better?
q.st: Ke eng se thusang moithuti ho utloisisa pale hamolemo?

options.en: Reading the story very quickly without thinking
options.st: Ho bala pale habualanyana ntle le ho nahana

options.en: Writing down only the difficult words of the story
options.st: Ho ngola mantsoe a thata a pale feela

options.en: Asking questions like 'Who?' and 'What is happening?'
options.st: Ho botsa lipotso joalo ka 'Ke mang?' le 'Ke eng se etsahalang?'

title.en: Greeting People According to Their Social Rank
title.st: Lumelisa Batho ho Latela Tlhahlamano

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Sesotho Syllabus p. 1, Outcome 9 (TG)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Sesotho Sehlopha sa 5 p. 1, Sepheo 9 (TG)

outcome.en: Greet people according to their hierarchy during a speech (lumelisa batho ho latela tlhahlamano ea bona ha ba etsa puo.)
outcome.st: lumelisa batho ho latela tlhahlamano ea bona ha ba etsa puo.

text.en: Basotho culture teaches us to respect everyone, especially elders and respected people. When greeting an older person, you say 'Lumela ntate' or 'Lumela 'm'e'. When greeting more than one person, you use 'Lumelang'. Showing respect in greetings is an important part of Basotho character.
text.st: Setso sa Basotho se re ruta ho hlompha batho bohle, haholo ba baholo le ba hlomphehang. Ha o lumelisa motho e moholo, o re 'Lumela ntate' kapa 'Lumela 'm'e'. Ha o lumelisa batho ba fetang ba babeli, o sebelisa 'Lumelang'. Ho hlompha ha morao ke karolo ea bohlokoa ea botho ba Mosotho.

text.en: When greeting a chief or a respected elder, you follow cultural customs. Men clap with their hands flat when greeting a chief. Women clap with cupped hands. Children bow slightly and say 'Lumela ntate' or 'Lumela 'm'e'. These ways show respect.
text.st: Ha o lumelisa morena kapa mosuoe, o kgomarela moetlo oa setso. Banna ba ithupa le litlhapi ha ba lumelisa morena. Basali ba ithupa le likhomo. Bana ba lumelisa ka ho ithupa fatshe le ho re 'Lumela ntate' kapa 'Lumela 'm'e'. Mekhoa ena e bontša hlompho.

text.en: Act out a greeting role-play at school. Ask one learner to play the role of a chief, an elder, a fellow learner, and a small child. Other learners greet each one in the correct way. Discuss how different roles require different greetings.
text.st: Etsa papali ea ho lumelisana ka sekolong. Kopa moithuti a bapale e le morena, mosuoe, moithuti, le ngoanana. Baithuti ba bang ba lumelise e mong le e mong ka tsela e nepahetseng. Bua le ba bang ba bang ka mekhoa e fapaneng ea ho lumelisa.

q.en: How does a child correctly greet their father?
q.st: Ngoana o lumelisa ntate oa hae ka tsela efe e nepahetseng?

options.en: 'Lumelang ntate' while clapping at their mouth
'Lumela ntate' while bowing slightly with respect
options.st: 'Lumela ntate' ka ho ithupa fatshe le ho hlompha
Ha a bue letho, a meme feela

title.st: Sebelisa Mantsoe a Tšoanang ka Moelelo (Mantsoe a Lekanang)

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Sesotho Syllabus p. 2, Outcome 21 (TG)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Sesotho Sehlopha sa 5 p. 2, Sepheo 21 (TG)

outcome.en: Use words with the same meaning in sentences (sebelisa mantsoe a tšoanang ka moelelo.)
outcome.st: sebelisa mantsoe a tšoanang ka moelelo.

text.en: Synonyms are different words that have the same or a very similar meaning. For example: 'The child is crying' — the words 'lela' and 'lla' have a similar meaning. Use synonyms in your sentences to make your language richer and more complete.
text.st: Mantsoe a lekanang ke mantsoe a fapaneng empa a nang le moelelo o tšoanang kapa o haufi. Ka mohlala: 'Ngoana o a lela' le 'Ngoana o a lla' — mantsoe 'lela' le 'lla' a na le moelelo o tšoanang. Sebelisa mantsoe a lekanang polelong ho etsa puo ea hao e be e monate le e phethahetseng.

text.en: Synonyms help us when we write or speak, so that we do not repeat the same word all the time. For example: 'motho e moholo' and 'mosuoe' have a similar meaning. Learning synonyms strengthens your Sesotho.
text.st: Mantsoe a lekanang a re thusa ha re ngola kapa re bua, hore re se ke ra pheta lefoko le le leng ka nako tsohle. Ka mohlala: 'motho e moholo' le 'mosuoe' li na le moelelo o haufi. 'Hara' le 'mahe' ho boleloa hore 'joala ka'. Ho ithuta mantsoe a lekanang ho matlafatsa Sesotho sa hao.

text.en: Write the following sentence on the board: 'Thabo is running' — then ask learners to find another Sesotho word with a similar meaning to 'qhela'. ('Thabo o a tšoha' is a correct answer.) Repeat this with three other words.
text.st: Ngola mantsoe a latelang hara patlo: 'Thabo o a qhela' — ebe o botsa baithuti ho fumana lefoko le leng la Sesotho le nang le moelelo o tšoanang le 'qhela'. ('Thabo o a tšoha' ke karabo e nepahetseng.) Etsa joalo ka mantsoe a mang a mararo.

q.en: Which word has a similar meaning to 'nyoloha' (to go up / rise)?
q.st: Ke lefoko lefe le nang le moelelo o tšoanang le 'nyoloha'?

title.en: Using a Noun as Subject or Object in a Sentence
title.st: Sebelisa Lereho e le Moetsi kapa Sehloohong sa Polelo

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Sesotho Syllabus p. 2, Outcome 28
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Sesotho Sehlopha sa 5 p. 2, Sepheo 28

outcome.en: Use a noun as subject or object in a sentence (sebelisa lereho e le moetsi kapa moetsuoa polelong.)
outcome.st: sebelisa lereho e le moetsi kapa moetsuoa polelong.

text.en: A noun is a word that names a thing, a person, a place, or an idea. For example: 'khomo' (cow), 'moithuti' (learner), 'thaba' (mountain), 'khotso' (peace). In a sentence, a noun can be a subject (who or what does the action) or an object (what the action is about). For example: 'The learner reads a book.' Here 'learner' is the subject, 'book' is the object.
text.st: Lereho ke lefoko le bolelaang ntho, motho, sebaka, kapa mohopolo. Ka mohlala: 'khomo', 'moithuti', 'thaba', 'khotso'. Polelong, lereho le ka ba sehloohong (moetsi oa ketso) kapa moetsi (seo ketso e amanang le sona). Ka mohlala: 'Moithuti o bala buka.' Mona 'moithuti' ke sehloohong, 'buka' ke moetsi.

text.en: Knowing the subject and object in a sentence helps us write correct sentences. Ask yourself: 'Who or what is doing the action?' — that is the subject. 'What is affected by the action?' — that is the object. For example: 'Father is chopping a tree.' — 'Father' is the subject, 'tree' is the object.
text.st: Ho tseba sehloohong le moetsi polelong ho re thusa ho ngola lipolelo tse nepahetseng. Botsa boitspreng: 'Ke mang ea etsang ketso?' — eo ke sehloohong. 'Ke ntho efe ea amehang?' — eo ke moetsi. Ka mohlala: 'Ntate o rema sefate.' — 'Ntate' ke sehloohong, 'sefate' ke moetsi.

text.en: Write three sentences on the board with the subject or object missing — such as 'O jesa ___.' or '___ e a bua.' Ask learners to fill in the correct noun. Then they explain whether that noun is a subject or an object.
text.st: Ngola lipolelo tse tharo hara patlo ntle le mantsoe a sehloohong kapa a moetsi — joalo ka 'O jesa ___.' kapa '___ e a bua.' Kopa baithuti ho tlatsa mantsoe a lereho a nepahetseng. Ebe ba hlalosa hore lereho leo ke sehloohong kapa ke moetsi.

q.en: In the sentence 'Grandmother cooks for the children', which word is the subject?
q.st: Polelong 'Nkhono o phehela bana', ke lefoko lefe le le sehloohong?

title.st: Sebelisa Sehokelo Lipolelong

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Sesotho Syllabus p. 2, Outcome 32
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Sesotho Sehlopha sa 5 p. 2, Sepheo 32

outcome.en: Use conjunctions in sentences (sebelisa sehokelo lipolelong.)
outcome.st: sebelisa sehokelo lipolelong.

text.en: A conjunction is a word that joins two sentences or parts of a sentence together. Common conjunctions in Sesotho are: 'le' (and), 'empa' (but), 'hobane' (because), 'ha' (when/if), and 'ebe' (then/and then). For example: 'I go to school and my sibling.' Here 'le' is the conjunction.
text.st: Sehokelo ke lefoko le hokelang lipolelo tse peli kapa likarolo tsa polelo hammoho. Lisehokelo tse tsebahalang ka Sesotho ke: 'le' (and), 'empa' (but), 'hobane' (because), 'ha' (when/if), le 'ebe' (then/and then). Ka mohlala: 'Ke ea sekolong le ngoaneso.' Mona 'le' ke sehokelo.

text.en: When we use conjunctions, we join two ideas into one sentence, making our language better and more complete. For example, instead of saying: 'I like porridge. I like water.' — you can join them by saying: 'I like porridge and water.' Or: 'I wanted to speak but I was afraid.'
text.st: Ha re sebelisa lisehokelo, re hokela manahano a mabeli polelong e le ngoe, 'me puo ea hoa ba botle le e phethahetseng. Ka mohlala, ho fapana le ho bua: 'Ke rata joala. Ke rata metsi.' — o ka hokela ka ho re: 'Ke rata joala le metsi.' Kapa: 'Ke ne ke batla ho bua empa ke ne ke tšaba.'

text.en: Give learners two short sentences — such as 'Lerato is singing' and 'Lerato is playing' — then ask them to join them using one conjunction. Discuss different ways they could use — 'le', 'empa', or 'hobane'.
text.st: Fa baithuti lipolelo tse peli tse khutshoane — joalo ka 'Lerato o a bina' le 'Lerato o a bapala' — ebe o ba kopa ho li hokela ka sehokelo se le seng. Bua le ba bang ka tsela tsela tse fapaneng tse ka sebelisotsoang — 'le', 'empa', kapa 'hobane'.

q.en: Which conjunction correctly joins these sentences: 'I was hungry ___ I ate.'?
q.st: Ke sehokelo sefe se hokelang lipolelo tsena hammoho: 'Ke ne ke lapile ___ ke eja.'?

outcome.st: ngola papatso.

text.en: Papatso ke mofuta oa mongolo o tsebisang sechaba ka thepa kapa tšebeletso e rekisoang. E hloka Sehlooho se seholo se khahlang mahlo, Tlhaloso ea boleng le molemo oa thepa (hore na e fapana joang le tse ling), Theko e hlakileng ka Maloti, le Moo e ka rekoang teng.

outcome.en: Use an idiophone indicating sound, smell, and colour (sebelisa sere se bontšang molumo, monko le ’mala.) and collective nouns (sebelisa mareho-’moka ka nepo lipolelong.)
outcome.st: sebelisa sere se bontšang molumo, monko le ’mala.; sebelisa mareho-’moka ka nepo lipolelong.

text.en: Sere ke lentsoe le ikhethileng la Sesotho le takang setšoantšo ka molumo kapa pono: "Ho re tu!" (khutsa ho se modumo), "Ho re phuu!" (monko o phallang), "Ho re thiri!" (ho otloloha joaloka tsela), Ho re putla! (ho robeha ha lehong). Mareho-’moka a hlalosa pokello: Mohlape oa linku, lekoko la batho.

text.en: Ask learners to utter the idiophone for when a stone splashes into the deep Senqu river: "Pshatla!" or "Tobere!"

outcome.en: Explain the wisdom and moral teachings inside popular Sesotho proverbs
outcome.st: Hlalosa bohlale le thuto e kahare ho maele a tummeng a Sesotho

text.en: Maele are traditional proverbs that summarize the life wisdom of our ancestors. For example: 'Kokoana-hloko e thiba lesoba' teaches that even small contributions matter. 'Pelo-nolo e aheletse' teaches the strength of gentleness and patience.
text.st: Maele ke lipolelo tsa bohlale tsa baholo-holo ba rona tse re fang tataiso bophelong. Mohlala: 'Kokoana-hloko e thiba lesoba' e ruta hore leha motho a le monyane kapa tlatsetso e le nyane, e na le bohlokoa. 'Pelo-nolo e aheletse' e ruta bohlokoa ba mosa le mamello.

text.en: Write three proverbs on the board. Let learners work in pairs to discuss what real-life school situations fit each proverb.
text.st: Ngola maele a mararo letlapeng. Lumella baithuti ho buisana ka bobeli hore na ke maemo afe a sekolo a lumellanang le maele ka mang.

text.en: Tsomo ea Sankatana e hlalosa sebōpuoa se bitsoang Khodumodumo se ileng sa metsa batho bohle le liphoofolo tsa lefatše. Ngoana e monyenyane ea bitsoang Sankatana o ile a hola ka sebete, a loantša Khodumodumo, a e phunya mpa ’me a lokolla sechaba sohle. E ruta ka boinehelo le sebete.

outcome.en: Write a cohesive descriptive essay in Sesotho using rich sensory vocabulary
outcome.st: Ngola tlhamo e hlalosang e monate o sebelisa mantsoe a hlakileng a kutlo

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Tlhamo e hlalosang e taka setšoantšo kelellong ea mmali. Sebelisa mantsoe a amang mahlo, litsebe, le nko: "Mosi o mosoeu o ne o kupa matlong a joang, ha likhomo li bokolla meluleng e batang ea noka." Qala ka kenyelletso, mmele oa tlhamo, le qetello e khahlisang.
text.st: Ha u ngola tlhamo e hlalosang ka Sesotho, taka setšoantšo se phelang ka mantsoe: Sebelisa tlotlontsoe ea mantsoe a hlalosang maikutlo, melumo le pono. Hlophisa serapa sa kenyelletso, lirapa tsa mmele, le qetello e nang le botsitso.

text.en: Have learners list at least five Sesotho adjectives before starting to write their draft.
text.st: Etsang hore baithuti ba ngole fatše maele kapa mantsoe a mane a hlalosang pele ba qala tlhamo.

q.en: Karolo ea pele ea tlhamo e hlahisang taba le ho hohela mmali e bitsoa eng?
q.st: Karolo ea pele ea tlhamo e hlahisang taba le ho hohela mmali e bitsoa eng?

title.en: Thuto ka Dingolwa tsa Sesotho: Thomas Mofolo
title.st: Thuto ka Dingolwa tsa Sesotho: Thomas Mofolo

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Understand the contribution of early Basotho authors like Thomas Mofolo
outcome.st: Kutloisiso ea bohlokoa ba bangoli ba pele ba Basotho ba kang Thomas Mofolo

text.en: Thomas Mofolo was a famous Mosotho writer born in Khojane. In 1925, he wrote the world-renowned historical novel 'Chaka', which has been translated into English, French, and German. Morija Museum & Archives and the Morija Printing Works played a vital role in publishing early African literature.
text.st: Thomas Mofolo e ne e le mongoli ea tummeng oa Mosotho ea hlahetseng Khojane. O ngotse buka e tummeng lefatšeng ea 'Chaka', e fetoletsoeng lipuong tse ngata tsa lefatše. Morija Printing Works le Morija Museum li bile le karolo e kholo ho hlahiseng lingoliloeng tsa pele tsa Afrika.

text.en: Discuss Morija's historic role as a center of printing, education, and culture in Lesotho since the 1800s.
text.st: Buisanang ka karolo ea nalane ea Morija e le setsi sa khatiso, thuto le meetlo Lesotho ho tloha lilemong tsa bo-1800.

q.en: Ke buka efe e tummeng ea nalane e ngotsoeng ke Thomas Mofolo e tsebahalang lefatšeng lohle?
q.st: Ke buka efe e tummeng ea nalane e ngotsoeng ke Thomas Mofolo e tsebahalang lefatšeng lohle?

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Linguistic & Literary Learning Area (Sesotho)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Conduct a formal dialogue using traditional honorifics and respectful vocabulary
outcome.st: Bua puisano ea semmuso o sebelisa puo ea tlhompho e loketseng baetapele

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Puong ea Sesotho, ha re bua le Morena kapa lekhotla, re sebelisa puo ea hlompho e phahameng: "Morena e Moholo", "Khotso Morena", "Re kopa ho beha taba kapel'a khotla la hao". Ha re sebelise mantsoe a boikhohomoso, re bontša boikokobetso le mamello.
text.st: Ha re bua le marena le makhotla a motse, Sesotho se laela hore re bue ka tlhompho: Re re "Khotso Morena", "Taba ea rona e eme tjena Morena". Puo ena ea seriti e boloka khotso le kutloano metseng ea rona.

text.en: Set up a mock village meeting (pitso) where learners present community development requests.
text.st: Hlophisang pitso ea motse phaposing moo baithuti ba hlahisang likopo tsa ntlafatso ea motse.

q.en: Ke tumeliso efe e nepahetseng le e nang le seriti ha u kena ka pel'a Morena lekhotleng la hae?
q.st: Ke tumeliso efe e nepahetseng le e nang le seriti ha u kena ka pel'a Morena lekhotleng la hae?

syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Linguistic & Literary (Sesotho)

outcome.en: Analyze philosophical proverbs guiding ethics, character, and integrity
outcome.st: Hlahloba maele a tebileng a laolang mekhoa, boitšoaro, le botšepehi

lessons.source: Lenaneo la Thuto la Motheo la Sesotho (MoET)

text.en: Maele a Sesotho ke letlotlo la mekhoa le melao ea botho. "Motho ke motho ka batho" e bolela hore bophelo le seriti sa motho li bōptjoa ke sechaba seo a phelang har'a sona. "Bitso lebe ke seromo" e lemosa hore lebitso le liketso tse mpe li ka u tlisetsa litsietsi.
text.st: Maele a Sesotho a re fa motheo oa Botho. "Motho ke motho ka batho" e re hopotsa hore ha ho motho ea ka phelang a le mong kantle ho sechaba. "Ha le fupeloe le se le tšolohetse" e ruta ho nahanisisa le ho hlokomela liphello tsa liketso tsa rona.

text.en: Discuss the concept of Botho/Ubuntu and how digital tools must serve the human community.
text.st: Buisanang ka mohopolo oa Botho le kamoo theknoloji e lokelang ho sebeletsa sechaba kateng.

q.en: Maele a tummeng a reng "Motho ke motho ka batho" a ruta eng ka setso sa Botho?
q.st: Maele a tummeng a reng "Motho ke motho ka batho" a ruta eng ka setso sa Botho?

options.st: Hore motho a iphelele a le mong

title.en: Making Clay Animals from River Soil
title.st: Ho Bōpa Liphoofolo ka Letsopa la Noka

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Mould simple animal figures using soft natural clay or dough
outcome.st: Bōpa libopeho tse bonolo tsa liphoofolo u sebelisa letsopa la tlhaho

text.en: In Lesotho, children have moulded clay cattle, sheep, and horses from riverbanks for generations. Clay is soft when wet and hardens when dried in the sun. It helps develop strong finger muscles and creative imagination.
text.st: Lesotho, bana ba na le nako e telele ba bōpa likhomo le lipere tsa letsopa mabopong a linoka. Letsopa le bonolo ha le le metsi ebe lea thatafala ha le omisoa ke letsatsi. Le matlafatsa menwana le boqapi.

text.en: Collect clean riverbed clay or make home dough using flour, salt, and water.
text.st: Kopang baithuti ho tšoara letsopa la noka kapa ho kopanya phofo le metsi ho bōpa.

q.en: What natural material from riverbanks is traditionally used by Basotho children to mould cattle and toy figures?
q.st: Ke thepa efe ea tlhaho e tsoang linokeng e sebelisoang ke bana ba Basotho ho bōpa likhomo tsa setso?

title.st: Ho Taka Lehae le Motse oa Heso

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Express personal observations through drawing and colouring buildings and hills
outcome.st: Bontša pono ea hao ka ho taka matlo le maralla a heno

text.en: Every village has its own beauty. We can draw our stone huts with thatched roofs, blue mountains in the background, green fields, and friendly pets. Using colour brings your drawing to life.
text.st: Motse o mong le o mong o motle ka tsela ea oona. Re ka taka matlo a majoe a ruletsoeng ka joang, lithaba tse putsoa ka morao, masimo a matala, le liphoofolo tsa lapeng.

text.en: Encourage learners to use natural charcoal or coloured chalk if crayons are scarce.
text.st: Baithuti ba ka sebelisa mashala a hloekileng kapa choko haeba mebala e le sieo.

q.en: What natural material was traditionally used to thatch roofs of Basotho rondavels (mokhoro)?
q.st: Ke thepa efe ea tlhaho e neng e sebelisoa ho rulela matlo a mokhoro ea Sesotho?

title.en: Clapping and Rhythm in Action Songs
title.st: Ho Opha Matsoho le Morethetho Lipineng

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Coordinate rhythmic clapping with singing traditional children’s songs
outcome.st: Kopanya ho opha matsoho le ho bina lipina tsa setso tsa bana ka morethetho

text.en: Music and dance bring joy to people. In action songs like "’Mè mphe mponeng", we clap hands in time with the beat and stamp our feet gently. Rhythm helps our body and mind work together.
text.st: Mino le motjeko li tlisa thabo. Lipineng tsa liketso tse kang "’Mè mphe mponeng", re opha matsoho ho latela morethetho le ho toboketsa maoto hantle. Morethetho o kopanya pelo le kelello.

text.en: Start with slow clapping, then speed up gradually as learners stay synchronized.
text.st: Qalang ka ho opha butle ebe le potlakisa morethetho hanyane ka hanyane.

q.en: What body action helps learners keep steady musical rhythm while singing together in class?
q.st: Ke ketso efe ea ’mele e thusang baithuti ho tšoara morethetho ha ba bina hammoho phaposing?

options.st: Ho lula u khutsitse u koetse mahlo
