title.en: Making Wire Cars and Reusable Toys
title.st: Ho Etsa Likoloi tsa Terata le Lintho tsa Papali

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Construct simple wire toy cars using discarded wire and bottle caps
outcome.st: Aha likoloi tsa terata u sebelisa lithapo le likhurumelo tsa makotikoti

text.en: Basotho children are famous for designing wire cars (likoloi tsa terata). Using clean scrap wire, shoe polish tins, and plastic bottle caps as wheels, young engineers create moving vehicles with steering handles.
text.st: Bana ba Basotho ba tumme haholo ka ho etsa likoloi tsa terata. Ba sebelisa lithapo tse lahliloeng, likhurumelo tsa libotlolo e le mabili, le litepisi tse thōtsehang ho tsamaisa koloi.

text.en: Ensure learners blunt sharp wire ends with pliers or fabric tape for safety.
text.st: Hlokomelang hore lintlha tse bohale tsa terata lia khopamisoa ho thibela ho hlaba.

q.en: What discarded household item is commonly recycled to make turning wheels for a homemade wire car?
q.st: Ke ntho efe ea lapeng e lahliloeng e sebelisoang ho etsa mabili a bilikang a koloi ea terata?

options.en: Plastic bottle lids or boot polish tins
options.st: Likhurumelo tsa libotlolo kapa tsa polish

title.en: Litema: Basotho Wall Murals and Geometric Patterns
title.st: Litema: Mekhabiso ea Mabota a Sesotho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Recreate traditional geometric Litema patterns found on Mosotho homesteads
outcome.st: Etsa mehlala ea litema tsa setso tse khabisang mabota a matlo a Sesotho

text.en: Litema is the traditional geometric art practiced by Basotho women to decorate home walls (seotloana). Using fingers and combs on wet dung and clay plaster, beautiful repeating diamond and zig-zag patterns are engraved before they dry.
text.st: Litema ke bonono ba bohlokoa ba basali ba Basotho ba ho khabisa mabota a matlo. Ba sebelisa menwana kapa likama holim'a bolokoe bo metsi ho hula mekhabiso ea litaemane le lithaba pele e oma.

text.en: Provide cardboard squares and let learners scratch geometric patterns using a blunt wooden stick.
text.st: Fanang ka likhatone baithuti ba tale litema ba sebelisa lehong le lerootho.

q.en: What is the name of the traditional Basotho geometric wall engraving art?
q.st: Ke lebitso la bonono ba Sesotho ba ho khabisa mabota ka mela le mekhabiso ea setso?

title.st: Mokotlana oa Ka oa Poloko ea Chelete

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Create a savings container and understand putting coins away for future needs
outcome.st: Etsa setshelo sa ho boloka chelete le ho utloisisa molemo oa ho boloka

text.en: Saving means keeping some money aside today for something important tomorrow. We can make a piggy bank from a clean tin can with a small slit cut into the lid. Even saving 50 lisente each week adds up to buy school pens.
text.st: Ho boloka ho bolela ho beha chelete e nyane thōko kajeno bakeng sa tlhokahalo ea hosane. Re ka etsa setshelo sa poloko ka lekotikoti le hloekileng. Ho boloka lisente tse 50 beke le beke ho reka lipene tsa sekolo.

text.en: Help learners calculate how many cents they save in a month if they save 20 cents every school day.
text.st: Balanang hore na ba ka ba le bokae ha ba boloka lisente tse 20 letsatsi le letsatsi ka khoeli.

q.en: Why is it wise to save small amounts of coins in a safe piggy bank at home?
q.st: Hobaneng ha ho le bohlale ho boloka chelete e nyane setshelong sa poloko lapeng?

options.en: To buy useful school materials or handle future emergencies
options.st: Ho reka thepa ea bohlokoa ea sekolo le bakeng sa litšohanyetso

options.en: So you can throw the money into the river
options.st: E le hore u e lahlele ka nokeng

options.en: Because coins expire if not kept in dark tins

title.st: Ho Loha Meseme le Lefielo la Mosea

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Identify weaving fibers (mosea, qobo) and weave a basic grass mat coaster
outcome.st: Tseba joang ba ho loha (mosea) le ho loha moseme o monyenyane

text.en: Grass weaving is an honoured traditional craft in Lesotho. Mosea grass is harvested from mountain ravines, dried in the shade, and woven into durable sleeping mats (moseme), storage baskets (seroto), and sweeping brooms (lefielo).
text.st: Ho loha ka joang ke mosebetsi oa bohlokoa oa matsoho Lesotho. Joang ba mosea bo khaoa lithabeng, bo omisoe moriting, ebe bo loha meseme ea ho lula, liroto tsa lijo, le mafielo a ho fiela.

text.en: Bring samples of dried mosea grass to class so learners can feel its tensile strength.
text.st: Tlisang joang ba mosea phaposing baithuti ba bone matla le thello ea bona ha bo lohoa.

q.en: Which indigenous grass is traditionally harvested in Lesotho to weave mats (moseme) and brooms?
q.st: Ke joang bofe ba tlhaho bo khaoang lithabeng tsa Lesotho ho loha meseme le mafielo?

title.st: Liletsa tsa Setso: Lesiba le Moropa

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Describe how the Lesiba string-wind instrument produces sound and its role with herdboys
outcome.st: Hlalosa kamoo lesiba le letsang kateng le karolo ea lona har'a balisana

text.en: The Lesiba is a unique Basotho musical instrument consisting of a curved wooden stick, horsehair string, and a flattened quill (feather). The player breathes in and out over the quill to vibrate the string. Herdboys play it to calm grazing herds.
text.st: Lesiba ke seletsa se ikhethileng sa Basotho se entsoeng ka lehlaka, khole ea pere le lesiba la nonyana. Sebapali se hema ka ho budula le ho hula moea lesibeng. Balisana ba le letsa ho khutsisa likhomo makhulong.

text.en: Show an audio or video clip of a skilled elder playing the Lesiba.
text.st: Bapallang baithuti molumo o ikhethileng oa lesiba ha le lelitsoe ke sebapali sa setso.

q.en: How does the player produce the vibrant resonant sound on a traditional Lesiba?
q.st: Sebapali se ntša molumo joang seletseng sa Lesiba sa setso?

options.en: By inhaling and exhaling air vigorously across the bird quill
options.st: Ka ho hula le ho budula moea holim'a lesiba la nonyana

options.en: By hitting it with heavy iron sticks
options.st: Ka ho le otla ka thupa ea tšepe

options.en: By plugging it into an electrical plug

topic.st: Serapa sa Sekolo e le Khoebo

title.st: Ho Lema le ho Rekisa Moroho oa Spinach

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Plan a small school vegetable bed and calculate simple sales from fresh bunches
outcome.st: Rala serapa sa meroho sekolong le ho bala chelete e kenang thekisong ea liphutheloana

text.en: Entrepreneurship means spotting an opportunity and taking action. If a school class prepares a vegetable plot with compost, waters spinach seeds, and harvests 20 fresh bunches selling at M5 each, the class earns M100 to purchase sports balls.
text.st: Bhoebi bo qala ka ho bona monyetla le ho nka bohato. Haeba phaposi e lema moroho oa spinach ka moquba, ea nosetsa ebe e kotula liphutheloana tse 20 tse rekisoang ka M5 e le 'ngoe, ba fumana M100 ea ho reka libolo tsa papali.

text.en: Integrate this with practical agriculture in the school yard using keyhole garden beds.
text.st: Kopanyang sena le lirapa tsa lifariki (keyhole gardens) lebaleng la sekolo.

q.en: If learners sell 15 bunches of garden spinach at M6 per bunch, how much money do they collect?
q.st: Haeba baithuti ba rekisa liphutheloana tse 15 tsa spinach ka M6 e le 'ngoe, ba bokella chelete e kae?

title.st: Mekhabiso ea Lifaha le Melumo ea Eona

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Design repeating geometric bead necklaces using traditional colour schemes
outcome.st: Rala meqhaka ea lifaha e nang le mebala ea setso sa Sesotho

text.en: Beadwork (lifaha) has adorned Basotho traditional dress for centuries. Different colours convey messages: white represents purity and peace, blue signifies rain and sky, and yellow represents warmth and sunshine. Crafting beadwork requires patience, counting, and pattern discipline.
text.st: Mesebetsi ea lifaha e khabisa liaparo tsa setso tsa Basotho. Mebala e na le meelelo: Bosoeu bo bolela khotso le bohloeki, boputsoa bo bolela pula le leholimo, mosehla o emela letsatsi le mofuthu. Ho etsa lifaha ho ruta mamello le ho bala.

text.en: Use colorful dry maize seeds or colored macaroni pasta for safe classroom stringing.
text.st: Sebelisang lithollo tsa poone tse mebala kapa macaroni e tšetsoeng mebala bakeng sa ho roka.

q.en: What does the colour white traditionally symbolize in Basotho beadwork and flags?
q.st: Mmala o mosoeu o emela eng ka setso sa Basotho lifaheng le folakeleng?

title.en: Spinning, Weaving, and Knitting with Lesotho Wool
title.st: Ho Oha le ho Roka ka Boea ba Linku le Lipoli

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Describe the journey of wool and mohair from shearing to woven tapestries and scarves
outcome.st: Hlalosa tsela ea boea ho tloha ho kutong ho isa ho meseme ea litšoantšo le li-scarf

text.en: Lesotho produces world-class Merino wool and Angora mohair. After spring shearing, the raw wool is washed, carded, and spun into thick yarn on spindles. Skilled craftswomen in Teyateyaneng and Maseru weave these into famous mohair tapestries and winter scarves for tourists.
text.st: Lesotho le hlahisa boea ba boleng bo phahameng ba Merino le pholetshe ea lipoli tsa Angora. Kamora kuto ea selemo, boea bo hlatsooa, bo ohiloe ka litšikere, ebe basali ba bōpa meseme e metle ea litšoantšo Teyateyaneng e rekisoang ho bahahlauli.

text.en: Mention the craft centers in Berea (TY) as practical examples of local cottage manufacturing.
text.st: Totobatsang litsi tsa bonono ba boea Teyateyaneng e le mehlala ea lifeme tsa lehae.

q.en: Which mountain district town in Lesotho is historically renowned for handwoven mohair tapestries and craft centers?
q.st: Ke toropo efe ea Lesotho e tsebahalang haholo ka ho loha meseme ea litšoantšo ea boea le litsi tsa bonono?

title.en: Creating Eye-Catching Posters to Sell Products
title.st: Ho Etsa Lipampiri tsa Papatso ea Lihlahisoa

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Design an informative commercial poster including product name, price, benefits, and location
outcome.st: Rala pampiri ea papatso e nang le lebitso la thepa, theko, molemo le sebaka

text.en: Marketing tells customers why they should buy your item. A good advertising poster needs a bold headline, clear picture, price in Maloti, where to find it, and what problem it solves (e.g., "Warm knitted wool beanies for winter - Only M25 at Grade 4 stall!").
text.st: Papatso e tsebisa bareki hore na ke hobaneng ba lokelang ho reka thepa ea hao. Pampiri e ntle ea papatso e hloka sehlooho se seholo, setšoantšo se hlakileng, theko ka Maloti, le moo e fumanehang teng (mohlala: "Likatiba tse mofuthu tsa boea tsa mariha - M25 feela!").

text.en: Have groups pin their posters on the wall and let classmates vote for the clearest advertisement.
text.st: Leketlisang lipampiri tsa papatso leboteng ebe baithuti ba voutela e hlakileng ka ho fetisisa.

q.en: What vital commercial detail must always be clearly written on an advertisement poster so buyers are informed?
q.st: Ke taba efe ea bohlokoa ea khoebo e lokelang ho ngoloa pampiring ea papatso e le hore bareki ba tsebe?

options.en: Price of the item and where to buy it
options.st: Theko ea thepa le moo e rekoang teng

title.en: Making Animals and Utensils with Paper Mache and Play Dough
title.st: Ho Etsa Liphoofolo le Lisebelisoa ka Pampiri le Mobu oa Lipapali

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Creativity Syllabus p. 144, Outcome 14 (Printed Note: Grade 6 page in G5 book)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la CEL Sehlopha sa 5 p. 144, Sepheo 14

outcome.en: use paper mache and play dough to make animals and household utensils.
outcome.st: Sebelisa paper mache le hlama ea ho bapala ho etsa liphoofolo le lintho tsa ka tlung.

text.en: Paper mache is made by mixing torn pieces of paper with a paste of flour and water. When it dries, it becomes hard and can be shaped into animals like cows, goats, or birds, and household utensils like bowls and pots. Play dough is a soft material made from flour, salt, water, and food colouring. It can be moulded easily into any shape while it is still soft.
text.st: Pampiri ea paper mache e etsoa ka ho tšoana likarolo tse nyenyane tsa pampiri le khofu ea bupi le metsi. Ha e omile, e phahama ebile e ka hlaoloa e be liphoofolo joalo ka likhomo, limphe kapa linonyana, le lisebelisoa tsa lapeng joalo ka liphia le likoto. Mobu oa lipapali ke ntho e bonolo e etsoa ka bupi, letsoai, metsi le mmala oa lijo. O ka hlaoloa habonolo o be sebopeho sepe ha o sa ntse o bonolo.

text.en: To make a paper mache animal: (1) Tear newspaper into small strips. (2) Mix flour and water into a smooth paste. (3) Dip the strips into the paste and layer them over a balloon or cardboard shape. (4) Let it dry completely, then paint it. Play dough animals are made by rolling, pinching, and pressing the dough into the shape you want.
text.st: Ho etsa phoofolo ea paper mache: (1) Khata pampiri ea koranta likarolo tse nyenyane. (2) Tšoana bupi le metsi ho fihlela ho ba khofu e bonolo. (3) Anya likarolo tse khofu ebe o li peta holim'a pono ea phefo kapa katong. (4) E lese e ome ka botlalo, ebe o e penta. Liphoofolo tsa mobu oa lipapali li etsoa ka ho phurolla, ho nyoolla le ho hatela mobu o be sebopeho seo o se batlang.

text.en: Bring in old newspapers and prepare a simple flour-and-water paste before class. Let learners work in pairs — one models the shape, the other applies paper strips. Display the finished animals around the classroom.
text.st: Tlisa likoranta tsa khale ebe o lokisa khofu e bonolo ea bupi le metsi pele ho sehloohong. Lumella baithuti ho sebetsa ka lijana — e mong o hlaola sebopeho, e mong o kenya likarolo tsa pampiri. Bontša liphoofolo tse phethiloeng kahohle ka phapusing.

q.en: What ingredients are needed to make paper mache paste?
q.st: Na ke lintho life tse hlokahalang ho etsa khofu ea paper mache?

title.en: Designing Warning Signs for Dangerous Places
title.st: Ho Rala Lipontšo tsa Tlhokomeliso Libakeng tse Kotsi

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Creativity Syllabus p. 144, Outcome 17 (Printed Note: Grade 6 page in G5 book)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la CEL Sehlopha sa 5 p. 144, Sepheo 17

outcome.en: design warning signs for dangerous places in their area.
outcome.st: Rala matšoao a temoso bakeng sa libaka tse kotsi tikolohong ea bona.

text.en: Warning signs tell people about danger so they can stay safe. Good warning signs use bold colours like red, yellow, and orange because these colours grab attention quickly. The message on a warning sign must be short and easy to understand. Common shapes for warning signs include triangles for danger and circles for rules. Examples of dangerous places that need warning signs include rivers, electrical boxes, construction sites, and cliffs.
text.st: Lipontšo tsa tlhokomeliso li bolella batho ka kotsi e le hore ba phele ba bolokehile. Lipontšo tse ntle tsa tlhokomeliso li sebelisa mebala e chesang joalo ka mofubelu, mmala oa mosehla le oa olorenji hobane mebala ena e hohela mahlo ka potlako. Molaetsa oa pontšo ea tlhokomeliso o tlameha ho ba mokopano le o utloahala habonolo. Mefuta ea lipono tsa lipontšo tsa tlhokomeliso e kenyelletsa li-triangle tsa kotsi le li-circle tsa melao. Mehlala ea libaka tse kotsi tse hlokang lipontšo tsa tlhokomeliso e kenyelletsa linoka, libokose tsa motlakase, libaka tsa kaho le maralla.

text.en: Take learners on a brief walk around the school to spot any dangerous areas (broken steps, exposed wires, steep slopes). Back in class, have each learner design a warning sign for one spot, using bold colours and simple symbols.
text.st: Nka baithuti ho ea tsamaea haufi le sekolo ho bona libaka tse kotsi (mahetla a robehileng, maili a bontšitsoeng, mathata a maatla). Ha le khutlile phapusing, leboellana baithuti ba rale pontšo ea tlhokomeliso ea sebaka se le seng, ka mebala e chesang le lipontšo tse bonolo.

q.en: Why are red, yellow, and orange most often used on warning signs?
q.st: Ke hobane'ng mofubelu, mosehla le olorenji li sebelisoa haholo lipontšong tsa tlhokomeliso?

options.en: They are the cheapest paint colours
options.st: Ke mebala e theko e tlase ea pente

options.en: They grab attention quickly and signal danger
options.st: E hohela mahlo ka potlako ebile e bontša kotsi

options.en: They are easy to find in nature

title.en: Reusing Plastics, Tins, and Bottles for Sustainability and Income
title.st: Ho Sebelisa Lipalasitiki, Likhantini le Libotlolong Bocha ho Tsehetsa Tikoloho le Lishoeshoe

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Creativity Syllabus p. 144, Outcome 24 (Printed Note: Grade 6 page in G5 book)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la CEL Sehlopha sa 5 p. 144, Sepheo 24

outcome.en: reuse plastics, tins and bottles to promote sustainable use of resources and generate income.
outcome.st: Sebelisa hape lipolasetiki, makotikoti le libotlolo ho khothaletsa tšireletso ea lisebelisoa le ho kenya chelete.

text.en: Reusing means using an item again instead of throwing it away. When we reuse plastics, tins, and bottles, we reduce rubbish in our communities and help the environment. At the same time, we can turn these materials into useful products that people will pay for. For example, plastic bottles can become flower pots or water containers; tins can be decorated and sold as pencil holders or storage containers; bottles can be made into lamps or vases.
text.st: Ho sebelisa bocha ho bolela ho sebelisa ntho hape ho e aho o lahlele. Ha re sebelisa lipalasitiki, likhantini le libotlolong bocha, re fokotsa marara sechaban le ho thusa tikoloho. Ka nako e ts'oanang, re ka fetoha lintho tsena tsa sebelisoa tse sebetsang tseo batho ba tla lefa ka tsona. Mohlala, libotlolong tsa palasitiki li ka ba lipoto tsa lipalesa kapa litenke tsa metsi; likhantini li ka ralisoa le ho rekisoa e le libokose tsa mapensele kapa lisebelisoa tsa polokelo; libotlolong li ka etsoa li-lamp kapa livase.

text.en: This practice is called upcycling — giving old, used items a new purpose and higher value. Upcycling helps protect the environment because fewer materials go into landfills. It also creates entrepreneurship opportunities: learners can make and sell upcycled products at school markets or in their communities to earn money.
text.st: Mokhoa ona o bitsoa upcycling — ho fa lintho tse khale, tse seng li sebelisitsoe morero o mocha le boleng bo phahameng. Upcycling e thusa ho sireletsa tikoloho hobane lintho tse fokolang li ea libakeng tsa marara. Hape e theha menyetla ea boiketlo: baithuti ba ka etsa le ho rekisa lihlahisoa tse upcyclileng memarakeng ea sekolo kapa sechaban ho fumana chelete.

text.en: Ask learners to bring one clean plastic bottle, tin, or glass bottle from home. In groups, they design and make a useful product from it. Hold a mini market at the end of the lesson where learners 'sell' their creations and explain the price and use to classmates.
text.st: Kopa baithuti ho tlisa botlolong e le ngoe e hloekisitsoeng ea palasitiki, khantini kapa botlolong ea galase ho tsoa lapeng. Ka lihlopha, ba rala le ho etsa sehlahisoa se sebetsang ho tsoa ho sona. Qeta sehloohong ka mmaraka o monyenyane moo baithuti ba 'rekisang' lihlahisoa tsa bona le ho hlalosa theko le tšebeliso ho baithuti ba bang.

q.en: What does 'upcycling' mean?
q.st: Na 'upcycling' e bolela eng?

options.en: Throwing away old items in a special bin
options.st: Ho lahlela lintho tse khale sebokoseng se khetheha

options.en: Turning used materials into new, more valuable products
options.st: Ho fetoha lintho tse seng li sebelitsoe tse ntša tse boleng bo phahameng

options.en: Buying new materials to replace old ones
options.st: Ho reka lintho tse ntša ho nkela tse khale sebaka

title.st: Mefuta ea Lits'ebelisoa

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Creativity Syllabus p. 145, Outcome 28 (Printed Note: Grade 6 page in G5 book)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la CEL Sehlopha sa 5 p. 145, Sepheo 28

outcome.en: explain different types of resources.
outcome.st: Hlalosa mefuta e fapaneng ea lisebelisoa.

text.en: A resource is anything that people use to meet their needs or make products. Resources can be grouped into three main types: (1) Natural resources — things found in nature, such as water, soil, trees, animals, minerals, and sunlight. (2) Human resources — the skills, knowledge, and effort that people bring to work, such as a teacher, a farmer, or a builder. (3) Capital resources — tools, machines, and buildings that people use to make other things, such as a tractor, a sewing machine, or a school building.
text.st: Lits'ebelisoa ke ntho efe kapa efe eo batho ba e sebelisang ho fihlela ditlhoko tsa bona kapa ho etsa lihlahisoa. Lits'ebelisoa li ka aroloa ka mefuta e meraro e meholo: (1) Lits'ebelisoa tsa tlhaho — lintho tse fumanehang tlhokomeliso, joalo ka metsi, mobu, lifate, liphoofolo, limela tsa lefats'e le leseli la letsatsi. (2) Lits'ebelisoa tsa batho — bokgoni, tsebo le boiketlo bo batho ba bo tlisang mosebetsing, joalo ka mosuoe, molemi kapa moahi. (3) Lits'ebelisoa tsa khapitale — lisebelisoa, metšene le meaho eo batho ba e sebelisang ho etsa lintho tse ling, joalo ka trekere, metšene ea ho rokha kapa moaho oa sekolo.

text.en: Draw three columns on the board labelled 'Natural', 'Human', and 'Capital'. Call out items one by one (e.g., a river, a carpenter, a hammer) and ask learners to come up and write each item in the correct column. Discuss any disagreements as a class.
text.st: Thala likholomo tse tharo lebordong tse ngotseng 'Tlhaho', 'Batho', le 'Khapitale'. Bitsa lintho tse le tse le tse (mohlala, noka, mosebi oa matsoho, hama) ebe o kopa baithuti ho tla ho ngola ntho nngwe le nngwe kholoming e nepahetseng. Bua ka menahano e fapaneng e le sehlopha.

q.en: Which of the following is a human resource?
q.st: Ke efe ea tse latelang e leng lits'ebelisoa tsa batho?

title.st: Lits'ebelisoa tse Khutlang le tse sa Khutleng

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Creativity Syllabus p. 145, Outcome 29 (TG) (Printed Note: Grade 6 page in G5 book)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la CEL Sehlopha sa 5 p. 145, Sepheo 29 (TG)

outcome.en: classify resources into renewable and non-renewable.
outcome.st: Arola lisebelisoa ho ba tse ntlafatsoang le tse sa ntlafatsoeng.

text.en: Renewable resources are resources that can be replaced naturally over time if we use them carefully. Examples include sunlight, wind, water, and trees (when replanted). Non-renewable resources are resources that cannot be replaced once they are used up — they took millions of years to form in the earth. Examples include coal, oil, natural gas, and minerals such as diamonds and gold. Because non-renewable resources will run out one day, it is important to use them wisely and to look for alternative energy sources like solar power.
text.st: Lits'ebelisoa tse khutlang ke lits'ebelisoa tse ka hlasoloang ke tlhaho nako le nako ha re li sebelisa ka kelello. Mehlala e kenyelletsa leseli la letsatsi, moea, metsi le lifate (ha li jalloa bocha). Lits'ebelisoa tse sa khutleng ke lits'ebelisoa tse ke keng tsa boeoa ha li se li sebelisitsoe — li nkile lilemo tse limilione ho hlaha lefats'eing. Mehlala e kenyelletsa koale, oli, gase ea tlhaho le limela tsa lefats'e joalo ka daemont le khauta. Hobane lits'ebelisoa tse sa khutleng li tla fela ka letsatsi le leng, ho bohlokoa ho li sebelisa ka bohlale le ho batlana le methopo e meng ea matla joalo ka matla a letsatsi.

text.en: Give learners a set of picture cards showing various resources (sun, coal, wind, oil, trees, gold). Have them sort the cards into two groups — Renewable and Non-Renewable — and justify each choice. Discuss as a class after sorting.
text.st: Fa baithuti sehlopha sa likhaththa tsa litšoantšo tse bontšang lits'ebelisoa tse fapaneng (letsatsi, koale, moea, oli, lifate, khauta). Ba kopele ho arola likhaththa ka lihlopha tse peli — Tse Khutlang le Tse sa Khutleng — le ho hlalosa khetho nngwe le nngwe. Bua ka taba eo e le sehlopha ka mor'a ho arola.

q.en: Which resource is non-renewable?
q.st: Ke lits'ebelisoa life tse sa khutleng?

title.en: Effects of Vandalism in Daily Life
title.st: Litlamorao tsa Vandaliseme Bophelong ba Letsatsi le Letsatsi

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Creativity Syllabus p. 145, Outcome 37 (Printed Note: Grade 6 page in G5 book)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la CEL Sehlopha sa 5 p. 145, Sepheo 37

outcome.en: identify effects of vandalism in daily life.
outcome.st: Hloaea litlamorao tsa tšenyo ea thepa (vandalism) bophelong ba letsatsi le letsatsi.

text.en: Vandalism means deliberately damaging or destroying property that belongs to other people or the community. Examples include breaking school windows, writing graffiti on walls, damaging water pipes, pulling out road signs, and burning public toilets. Vandalism is harmful because it damages resources that everyone needs. When a school window is broken, learners may feel cold and unsafe. When water pipes are damaged, families have no clean water. The community then has to spend money to repair the damage instead of using that money to build new schools or clinics.
text.st: Vandaliseme e bolela ho senya kapa ho bolaea thepa ea batho ba bang kapa ea sechaba ka boomo. Mehlala e kenyelletsa ho qhaqha mafensetere a sekolo, ho ngola grafiti marakong, ho senya makoatleng a metsi, ho tlosa lipontšo tsa tsela le ho chesa litoale tsa sechaba. Vandaliseme e kotsi hobane e senya lits'ebelisoa tseo bohle ba li hlokang. Ha fensetere ea sekolo e qhaqhiloe, baithuti ba ka ikutloa ba tsekama le ba se bolokehile. Ha makoatleng a metsi a sentsoe, malapa ha a fumane metsi a hloekisitsoeng. Sechaba se tlameha ho sebelisa chelete ho bapisoa mosebetsi oa tšenyo ho e aho ke ho sebelisa chelete eo ho haha likolo tse ntša kapa likeliniki.

text.en: Everyone has a responsibility to protect community property. We can prevent vandalism by reporting damage when we see it, taking care of shared spaces, educating others about the harm of vandalism, and being proud of our community resources. Looking after our resources helps the whole community to thrive.
text.st: Bohle ba na le maikarabelo a ho sireletsa thepa ea sechaba. Re ka thibela vandaliseme ka ho hlahisa tšenyo ha re e bona, ho hlokomela libaka tse abelanang, ho ruta ba bang ka kotsi ea vandaliseme, le ho ikantlha ka lits'ebelisoa tsa sechaba sa rona. Ho hlokomela lits'ebelisoa tsa rona ho thusa sechaba sohle ho phela hantle.

text.en: Show learners photos or drawings of vandalized vs. well-maintained community spaces (school, clinic, park). Ask: 'How does each place make you feel? Who is affected?' Lead a short discussion on community responsibility, then have learners write or draw one action they will take to protect their school.
text.st: Bontša baithuti litšoantšo kapa meqoqo ea libaka tsa sechaba tse sentsioeng kapa tse hlokometsoeng hantle (sekolo, keliniki, tšimo ea lipapali). Botsa: 'Sebaka seng le seng se o etsa o ikutloe joang? Ke mang ea amehang?' Etella pele puisano e khutshoane ka maikarabelo a sechaba, ebe o kopa baithuti ho ngola kapa ho thala ketso e le ngoe eo ba tla e nka ho sireletsa sekolo sa bona.

q.en: When water pipes in a community are vandalised, what is the most likely immediate effect?
q.st: Ha makoatleng a metsi a sechaban a sentsoa ke vandaliseme, ke litlamorao life tse ka etsahalang hang hang?

options.st: Sechaba se fumana pula e ngata

options.en: Families have no access to clean water
options.st: Malapa ha a kene metsi a hloekisitsoeng

options.en: Roads in the area get repaired

title.en: Pitch, Duration, and Volume of Environmental Sounds
title.st: Bophahamo, Nako, le Matla a Melumo ea Tlhaho

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Creativity Syllabus p. 144, Outcome 11 (TG) (Printed Note: Grade 6 page in G5 book)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la CEL Sehlopha sa 5 p. 144, Sepheo 11 (TG)

outcome.en: differentiate between the pitch, duration and volume of different sounds from the environment.
outcome.st: Khaohanya lipakeng tsa pitch, bolelele le molumo oa melumo e fapaneng tikolohong.

text.en: Every musical sound has three characteristics: Pitch is how high (like a bird chirping) or low (like a cow mooing) the note sounds. Duration is how long or short the sound echoes. Volume is how loud (thunder clapping) or soft (whispering breeze) the wave is.
text.st: Molumo o mong le o mong o na le mekhoa e meraro: Bophahamo (Pitch) ke kamoo molumo o phahameng joaloka nonyana kapa o tebileng joaloka khomo e bokollang. Nako (Duration) ke hore na molumo o nka nako e telele kapa e khutšoanyane. Matla (Volume) ke hore na o lerata kapa o lerootho joaloka moea.

text.en: Strike a metal triangle versus a heavy bass drum skin to let learners feel low vibration resonance.
text.st: Otla tšepe e tšesane ebe u bapisang le meropa ea matlalo ho utloa phapang ea melumo e tebileng.

q.en: Which environmental sound has a deep, LOW PITCH and a LOUD VOLUME?
q.st: Ke molumo ofe oa tlhaho o nang le molumo o tebileng (Low Pitch) le lerata le leholo (Loud Volume)?
q.sn: Molumo oa sealiba sa leholimo (thunder) o tebile haholo ebile o lerata le tšosang.

options.en: A heavy rolling thunderstorm clap (Sealiba sa leholimo)
A tiny cricket chirping in the grass
A quiet whisper in the classroom

title.en: Producers, Consumers, and Determining Fair Prices
title.st: Bahlahisi, Bareki, le ho Beha Litheko Tse Loketseng

syllabusRef.en: LCDC Grade 5 Creativity Syllabus p. 145, Outcomes 33, 34, 35 (TG) (Printed Note: Grade 6 page in G5 book)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la CEL Sehlopha sa 5 p. 145, Lipheo 33, 34, 35 (TG)

outcome.en: distinguish between producers and providers of goods and services.; describe a consumer of goods and services.; determine the price of goods and services.
outcome.st: Khaohanya bahlahisi le bafani ba thepa le litšebeletso, hlalosa moreki, le ho rala theko.

text.en: A Producer creates or grows goods (like a farmer growing potatoes or a carpenter making wooden desks). A Consumer is someone who buys and uses those goods. To set a fair price, the producer calculates the cost of raw materials and labor, adding a modest markup for sustainable profit.
text.st: Mohlahisi (Producer) ke motho ea lemang kapa a bōpang thepa (joaloka molemi oa litapole kapa moahi oa litafole). Moreki (Consumer) ke motho ea rekang thepa eo ho e sebelisa. Ho beha theko e loketseng, mohlahisi o kopanya litšenyehelo tsa thepa le matla a hae ebe o kenya puzo e lekaneng.

text.en: Simulate a classroom farmers market: Have learners calculate if selling 10 cabbages grown from M20 seeds at M8 each yields a fair living profit.
text.st: Balisang thekiso ea meroho: Haeba lipeo li jele M20 ’me u rekisitse likhabeche tse 10 ka M8 e le ’ngoe (M80), puzo ke M60.

q.en: What is the role of a consumer in an economic market?
q.st: Karolo ea moreki (consumer) khoebong ea motse ke efe?
q.sn: Moreki o reka thepa le lits'ebeletso tse hlahisitsoeng ke balemi le borakhoebo.

options.en: To purchase, consume, and utilize goods and services
options.st: Ho reka le ho sebelisa thepa le lits'ebeletso

options.en: To forbid anyone from trading at the market
options.st: Ho thibela batho ho reka setaleng

options.en: To destroy harvest crops in the fields

title.st: Ho Thala Litšoantšo tsa Lifahleho ka Matsoho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Use proportions to draw facial portraits using freehand sketching
outcome.st: Sebelisa litekanyo ho thala lifahleho ka matsoho

text.en: When sketching a face, divide the oval head in half: the eyes sit along the middle horizontal line. The tip of the nose is halfway between the eyes and the chin. The mouth is halfway between the nose and the chin. Using light pencil lines helps you adjust proportions easily.
text.st: Ha u thala sefahleho, arola sebopeho sa hlooho ka halofo: mahlo a lula moleng o bohareng. Ntlha ea nko e lula bohareng pakeng tsa mahlo le selelu. Molomo o bohareng pakeng tsa nko le selelu. Ho sebelisa mela e bobebe ea pensele ho u thusa ho lokisa habonolo.

text.en: Have learners pair up, sit opposite each other, and sketch each other's portraits focusing on eye and nose spacing.
text.st: Lumella baithuti ho lula ka bobeli ba shebane, 'me ba thalane lifahleho ba shebile libaka tsa mahlo le nko.

q.en: Where do the eyes naturally sit when drawing a human face in proportion?
q.st: Mahlo a lula hokae ka tlhaho ha ho thaloa sefahleho ka tekanyo?

options.en: About halfway down the head from the top
options.st: Hoo e ka bang bohareng ba hlooho ho tloha holimo

options.en: At the very top of the forehead

title.en: Tanning Hides and Crafting Traditional Leather Goods
title.st: Ho Suka Matlalo le ho Etsa Thepa ea Letlalo

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Explain the traditional tanning process (ho suka) and modern leather crafting
outcome.st: Hlalosa mokhoa oa ho suka matlalo le ho bōpa thepa ea letlalo

text.en: Traditional leather working (ho suka letlalo) involves scraping raw cow or sheep hides, softening them with natural plant oils, and rubbing them repeatedly until supple. From leather, artisans craft traditional shoes (likatiba/liriba), whips (lisebeletso), and sturdy drum skins.
text.st: Ho suka matlalo ke mosebetsi oa bohlokoa oa matsoho oa khale. Letlalo la khomo kapa nku lea hloekisoa, le tšoloe mafura a tlhaho, ’me le sukoe ka matsoho ho fihlela le le bonolo haholo. Le etsa lieta tsa letlalo, marapo a lipere, le matlalo a meropa.

text.en: Discuss how traditional leatherwork provides rural livelihoods without requiring expensive electric machinery.
text.st: Buisanang kamoo mesebetsi ea letlalo e phelisang malapa a mahaeng ntle le metjhini e turang.

q.en: What traditional process is used in Lesotho to turn raw animal hide into soft, workable leather?
q.st: Ke ts'ebetso efe ea setso e fetolang letlalo le thata la phoofolo hore le be bonolo le ho sebetsa?

options.en: Ho suka letlalo (traditional tanning and rubbing)

options.st: Ho le penta ka oli ea koloi

title.en: Simple Cash Book: Income, Expenses, and Net Balance
title.st: Buka ea Lichelete: Chelete e Kenang le e Tsoang

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Maintain a two-column cash book recording financial transactions for a school cooperative
outcome.st: Boloka tlaleho ea chelete e kenang le e tsoang bakeng sa khoebo e nyane

text.en: To run a successful enterprise, you must write down every transaction. Income is money coming in from sales. Expenses are money spent on stock or materials. Net Balance = Total Income - Total Expenses. Keeping clear records prevents money loss and cheating.
text.st: E le hore khoebo e atlehe, o tlameha ho ngola tšebelisano e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe fatše. Chelete e kenang (Income) e tsoa thekisong. Chelete e tsoang (Expenses) e reka thepa. Tekanyo e Salang = Chelete e Keneng - Chelete e Tsoileng. Tlaleho e hlakileng e thibela boshodu le tahlehelo.

text.en: Provide a sample weekly ledger sheet and let learners balance the books for a fruit stall.
text.st: Fanang ka pampiri ea tlaleho ea beke le beke baithuti ba bale chelete e keneng le e saletseng setaleng.

q.en: A young baker earns M250 from selling buns, but spent M150 on flour and sugar. What is the net profit balance?
q.st: Moapehi o fumane M250 thekisong ea makoenya, empa o ile a sebelisa M150 phofong le tsoekereng. Puzo e setseng ke bokae?

title.en: Planning and Starting a Small Enterprise
title.st: Ho Rala le ho Qala Khoebo e Nyane

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Draft a simple business plan: costs, pricing, customers, and profit
outcome.st: Rala moralo o bonolo oa khoebo: litšenyehelo, theko, bareki le phaello

text.en: A successful business starts with a plan. You must know: (1) Product (what are you making?), (2) Cost of materials (expenses), (3) Selling price, and (4) Profit: Profit = Selling Price − Expenses. Selling homemade scones, knitted scarves, or woven grass mats can generate income for young entrepreneurs.
text.st: Khoebo e atlehileng e qala ka moralo. U tlameha ho tseba: (1) Sehlahisoa (u etsa eng?), (2) Litšenyehelo tsa thepa, (3) Theko ea ho rekisa, le (4) Phaello: Phaello = Theko ea Thekiso − Litšenyehelo. Ho rekisa likuku, likatiba tse lohiloeng kapa meseme ho ka tlisetsa bo-rakhoebo ba banyenyane chelete.

text.en: Ask groups to calculate the cost to bake 10 scones (flour, sugar, oil) and determine the price per scone to make a fair profit.
text.st: Kopa lihlopha ho bala litšenyehelo tsa ho baka likuku tse 10 'me li fumane theko ka 'ngoe ho etsa phaello e ntle.

q.en: If it costs M20 to make 10 scones and you sell them all for M40, what is your profit?
q.st: Haeba ho u jella M20 ho etsa likuku tse 10 'me u li rekisa kaofela ka M40, phaello ea hao ke bokae?

title.en: Mobile Money in Lesotho: M-Pesa and EcoCash
title.st: Chelete ea Mohala: M-Pesa le EcoCash

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Explain how mobile money transforms payments, savings, and trade across rural Lesotho
outcome.st: Hlalosa kamoo chelete ea mohala e fetotseng tefo le khoebo metseng ea mahaeng Lesotho

lessons.source: Central Bank of Lesotho / ICT4D Curriculum

text.en: In Lesotho, many rural villages have no physical bank branches. Mobile money services like Vodacom M-Pesa and Econet EcoCash allow citizens to deposit, send money to relatives, pay school fees, buy electricity tokens, and receive business payments securely using even simple non-smartphone mobile phones.
text.st: Lesotho, metse e mengata ea mahaeng ha e na libanka. Lits'ebeletso tsa chelete ea mohala tse kang M-Pesa le EcoCash li lumella sechaba ho boloka chelete, ho e romela ho ba lelapa, ho patala litefiso tsa sekolo, le ho reka motlakase ba sebelisa mehala e tloaelehileng.

text.en: Discuss the ICT4D dimension: how mobile infrastructure bridges geographic barriers and banking divides.
text.st: Buisanang ka ICT4D: kamoo mehala e felisang tšitiso ea sebaka le bofuma ba lits'ebeletso tsa lichelete.

q.en: What major financial inclusion problem in mountainous rural Lesotho did mobile money (M-Pesa / EcoCash) help solve?
q.st: Ke bothata bofe bo boholo ba lichelete mahaeng a lithaba ba Lesotho boo chelete ea mohala e thusitseng ho bo rarolla?

options.en: Lack of formal bank branches in remote villages
options.st: Ho se be le libanka libakeng tse ka thōko tsa lithaba

options.en: Lack of salt and sugar in local shops

title.en: Drafting a Micro-Business Plan and Customer Care
title.st: Ho Rala Moralo oa Khoebo le Tlhokomelo ea Bareki

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Creativity & Entrepreneurial Learning Area
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Boqapi le Boithomelo

outcome.en: Develop a simple 1-page business proposal adhering to ethical business principles
outcome.st: Rala moralo oa leqephe le le leng oa khoebo o latelang melao ea boitšoaro e metle

text.en: A business plan explains what you will sell, who your target customers are, where you will operate, your startup costs, and projected profits. Honesty, fair pricing, clean hygiene, and treating customers with dignity are what sustain a business over the long run.
text.st: Moralo oa khoebo o hlalosa hore na u tla rekisa eng, bareki ba hao ke bo-mang, u tla sebetsa kae, thepa e qalang e ja bokae, le puzo e lebelletsoeng. Botšepehi, theko e lekaneng, bohloeki, le ho tšoara bareki ka seriti ke tsona tse ts'oarellang khoebo.

text.en: Help learners present their 1-page business plan to a mock panel of village community investors.
text.st: Thusang baithuti ho hlahisa meralo ea bona ea khoebo kapel'a sehlopha sa matsete a motse.

q.en: Which ethical quality is most important for a young entrepreneur to build lasting trust with community customers?
q.st: Ke boleng bofe ba boitšoaro bo bohlokoa ka ho fetisisa hore mohoebi a hahe tšepo e tšoarellang le bareki ba motse?

options.en: Honesty, fair weights, and courteous customer service
options.st: Botšepehi, litekanyo tse nepahetseng, le tšebeletso e nang le tlhompho

options.en: Overcharging customers whenever they are in a rush
options.st: Ho biza theko e phahameng ha bareki ba potlakile

options.en: Selling spoiled goods and refusing to refund

title.en: My Feelings: Happy, Sad, and Calm
title.st: Maikutlo a Ka: Thabo, Masoabi, le Khotso

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Identify basic emotional feelings and express them safely
outcome.st: Tseba maikutlo a mantlha le ho a hlahisa ka mokhoa o sireletsehileng

text.en: We all have feelings inside our hearts. Sometimes we feel happy when playing with friends. Sometimes we feel sad or frightened. It is good to talk to your teacher or parents when you feel worried.
text.st: Kaofela re na le maikutlo ka lipelong tsa rona. Ka nako e 'ngoe re thaba ha re bapala le metsoalle. Ka nako e 'ngoe re utloa bohloko kapa tšabo. Ho molemo ho bolella tichere kapa batsoali ha u tšoenyehile.

text.en: Have learners make happy, sad, and calm facial expressions in circle time.
text.st: Kopang baithuti ho bontša lifahleho tsa thabo le tsa masoabi selikeng sa phaposi.

q.en: What is a healthy thing to do when you feel sad, hurt, or frightened at school?
q.st: Ke ntho efe e phetseng hantle eo u lokelang ho e etsa ha u utloa bohloko kapa tšabo sekolong?

options.en: Talk to a trusted teacher or parent
options.st: Bolella tichere kapa motsoali eo u mo tšepang
Otla bana ba bang ka bohale

options.en: Hide in danger alone without telling anyone
options.st: Ipate u le mong ntle le ho bolella mang kapa mang

title.st: Ho Arolelana le ho Hlokomelana

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Demonstrate sharing and gentle actions towards peers
outcome.st: Bontša mosa le ho arolelana thepa le bana ba bang

text.en: Kindness makes our classroom a peaceful home. If a classmate does not have a pencil or forgets their lunch, sharing with them brings joy. A kind child says gentle words and includes everyone in games.
text.st: Mosa o etsa hore phaposi ea rona e be lehae la khotso. Haeba moithuti-’moho a se na pensele kapa a lebetse lijo, ho arolelana le eena ho tlisa thabo. Ngoana ea nang le mosa o bua mantsoe a monate le ho bapala le bohle.

text.en: Create a "Kindness Tree" on the board where learners stick leaves when they help a friend.
text.st: Etsang "Sefate sa Mosa" letlapeng moo baithuti ba behang makhasi ha ba thusitse motsoalle.

q.en: How can you show kindness when a classmate drops their pencils on the floor?
q.st: U ka bontša mosa joang ha moithuti-’moho a lihela lipensele fatše?

options.en: Help them pick up the pencils with a smile
options.st: Mo thuse ho thola lipensele ka pososelo

options.en: Laugh and step on the pencils
options.st: Tšeha ebe u li gata ka maoto

options.en: Take the pencils and keep them for yourself

title.en: Being Thankful for Nature and Sun
title.st: Ho Leboha Tlhaho le Letsatsi

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 1 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 1 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Appreciate the beauty of creation, morning sunlight, and clean water
outcome.st: Ananela botle ba tlholeho, khanya ea letsatsi, le metsi a hloekileng

text.en: Every morning when the sun rises over our Lesotho mountains, we breathe fresh air and see blue skies. Having gratitude in our hearts for life, family, and nature gives us peace and spiritual strength.
text.st: Hoseng ho hong le ho hong ha letsatsi le chaba holim'a lithaba tsa Lesotho, re hema moea o hloekileng le ho bona maru a matle. Ho ba le teboho lipelong tsa rona bakeng sa bophelo, lelapa le tlhaho ho re fa matla a moea le khotso.

text.en: Take a quiet moment of reflection in the morning where each child names one thing they are grateful for.
text.st: Etsang motsotso o khutsitseng hoseng moo ngoana ka mong a bolelang ntho e le 'ngoe eo a e lebohang.

q.en: What positive feeling do we cultivate when we say thank you for food and life?
q.st: Ke maikutlo afe a matle ao re a holisang ha re leboha lijo le bophelo?

options.st: Teboho, boikokobetso, le khotso ea pelo

title.st: Ho Hlompha Baholo, Matichere le Lithaka

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Practice courteous speech and respectful manners in community interactions
outcome.st: Sebelisa mekhoa e metle le puo e nang le tlhompho sechabeng

text.en: In Basotho culture, respect (tlhompho) is the foundation of character. We greet elders with two hands, use respectful titles ("Ntate", "’Mè"), listen when others speak, and knock before entering a room.
text.st: Moetlong oa Basotho, tlhompho ke motheo oa botho. Re lumelisa batho ba baholo ka matsoho a mabeli, re sebelisa litlotla tse kang "Ntate" le "’Mè", re mamela ha ba bang ba bua, ’me re kokota pele re kena ka tlung.

text.en: Role-play greeting an elder passing on the village path using both hands.
text.st: Bapallang kamoo ngoana a lumelisang motho e moholo tseleng ka matsoho a mabeli.

q.en: In Lesotho tradition, how do children receive an item or greet an elder to demonstrate deep respect?
q.st: Moetlong oa Lesotho, bana ba amohela ntho kapa ho lumelisa motho e moholo joang ho bontša tlhompho e tebileng?

options.en: Using both hands together with bowed head
options.st: Ka matsoho a mabeli a kopaneng u inamisitse hlooho

options.en: With one hand in your pocket looking away
options.st: Ka letsoho le le leng le le ka pokothong

options.en: By snatching it quickly and running
options.st: Ka ho e hula ka potlako ebe oa matha

title.en: Caring for My Body as a Sacred Gift
title.st: Ho Hlokomela ’Mele oa Ka e le Mpho e Halalelang

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Demonstrate understanding that our bodies are special and deserve clean care and safety
outcome.st: Utloisisa hore ’mele ke oa bohlokoa ebile o hloka bohloeki le tšireletso

text.en: Your body is precious. Keeping it clean by bathing, brushing your teeth, and wearing neat clothes keeps you healthy and confident. Remembering that your body belongs to you helps you keep it safe from harm.
text.st: ’Mele oa hao ke oa bohlokoa haholo. Ho o hloekisa ka ho hlapa, ho hlatsoa meno, le ho apara liaparo tse makhethe ho u fa bophelo bo botle le boits'epo. Ho tseba hore ’mele ke oa hao ho u thusa ho o sireletsa kotsing.

text.en: Teach the "Praise Your Body" routine: clean teeth, clean nails, neat hair, bright eyes.
text.st: Rutang litho tsa bohlokoa: meno a masoeu, manala a khutšoanyane a hloekileng, moriri o kutiloeng hantle.

q.en: Why is it important to brush your teeth every morning and evening?
q.st: Hobaneng ha ho le bohlokoa ho hlatsoa meno hoseng le mantsiboea?

options.en: To keep teeth strong, clean, and free of pain and decay
options.st: Ho boloka meno a matla, a hloekile ’me a se na libōkō kapa bohloko

options.en: So that you can eat sugar all day without water
options.st: E le hore u je tsoekere letsatsi lohle

options.en: It does not matter, baby teeth will fall anyway
options.st: Ha ho na taba ho hang

title.st: Ho Bapala ka Toka le ho Fana ka Monyetla

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 2 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 2 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Apply fairness and honesty when playing games with peers
outcome.st: Sebelisa toka, botšepehi, le ho fana ka menyetla ha u bapala le ba bang

text.en: Playing games like skipping rope (khoele) or football is fun when everyone follows the rules. Cheating or fighting ruins the game. When someone loses, we shake hands and encourage them to try again next time.
text.st: Ho bapala lipapali tse kang ho tlola khoele kapa bolo ea maoto ho monate ha bohle ba latela melao. Ho qhekella kapa ho loana ho senya papali. Ha motho a hlōtsoe, re mo ts'oara ka letsoho le ho mo khothalletsa.

text.en: Practice a game where learners take turns holding a ball for 10 seconds before passing smoothly.
text.st: Bapallang papali ea ho nehelana ka bolo ka tatellano ntle le ho qhanyetsana.

q.en: What should a good sportsperson do after their team loses a friendly school match?
q.st: Motho ea nang le moea o motle oa papali o lokela ho etsa eng kamora hore sehlopha sa hae se hloloe papaling?

options.en: Congratulate the winning team politely and practice more
options.st: Bolella bahloli hantle ’me u ikoetlise haholoanyane

options.en: Refuse to talk to friends ever again
options.st: Hana ho bua le metsoalle hape

title.en: The Meaning of Botho in Daily Life
title.st: Moelelo oa Botho Bophelong ba Letsatsi le Letsatsi

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Explain and demonstrate the core values of Botho (compassion, solidarity, integrity)
outcome.st: Hlalosa le ho bontša litšiea tsa Botho (qenehelo, kutloano, le botšepehi)

text.en: Botho is the golden principle of the Basotho: "Motho ke motho ka batho" (A person is a person through other people). Botho means welcoming strangers, helping vulnerable neighbors, showing sympathy when someone grieves, and acting with truthfulness.
text.st: Botho ke motheo oa boikhohomoso oa Basotho: "Motho ke motho ka batho". Botho bo bolela ho amohela baeti ka mofuthu, ho thusa mafutsana le batsofe, ho utloela ba saretsoeng bohloko, le ho phela ka nnete.

text.en: Ask learners how their families welcome a weary traveler walking through the village.
text.st: Botsang baithuti hore na malapeng a bona ba etsa joang ha moeti a fihla a khathetse.

q.en: Which action best reflects the Basotho traditional virtue of Botho?
q.st: Ke ketso efe e bontšang motheo oa tlhaho oa Botho moetlong oa Basotho?

options.en: Carrying a heavy water bucket for an elderly grandmother
options.st: Ho jarisa nkhono ea tsofetseng nkho e boima ea metsi

options.en: Boasting about having more shoes than classmates
options.st: Ho ithorisa ka lieta ho feta bana ba bang

options.en: Ignoring someone who falls down and hurt themselves
options.st: Ho iphapanyetsa motho ea oeleng fatše

title.st: Bohlokoa ba ho Bua Nnete ka Linako Tsohle

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Recognize the courage needed to admit mistakes and build trust
outcome.st: Hlokomela sebete sa ho ipolela liphoso le ho haha tšepo

text.en: Truth is like light. When you break a cup by accident, it takes courage to tell your mother the truth. When you tell lies, you have to tell more lies to cover it up, and people lose trust in you. Honesty brings peace of mind.
text.st: Nnete e joaloka khanya. Haeba u pshatla kopi ka phoso, ho hloka sebete ho bolella ’mè nnete. Ha u bua leshano, u tlameha ho qapa mashano a mangata ho le pata, ’me batho ba lahla tšepo ho uena. Nnete e tlisa khotso kelellong.

text.en: Share the famous folklore of the boy who cried wolf ("Molisana ea neng a hoeletse phokojoe").
text.st: Phetang tsomo ea molisana ea neng a qapa leshano la phokojoe ho fihlela batho ba sa mo tšepe.

q.en: What happens when a child consistently tells the truth, even when they made an accidental mistake?
q.st: Ho etsahala eng ha ngoana a bua nnete ka mehla, leha a entse phoso ka ts'ohanyetso?

options.en: People trust, respect, and forgive them
options.st: Batho ba mo tšepa, ba mo hlompha ’me ba mo tšoarela

options.en: Nobody will ever speak to them again
options.st: Ha ho motho ea tla bua le eena

title.st: Ho Rarolla Liqabang Ntle le Ntoa

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 3 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 3 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Apply calm communication to settle disputes among friends peacefully
outcome.st: Sebelisa lipuisano tse khutsitseng ho rarolla liqabang ka khotso

text.en: King Moshoeshoe I taught us: "Khotso ke khoro" (Peace is the gateway to prosperity). When you disagree with a friend, step back, take three deep breaths, speak calmly, and listen to their side. If needed, ask a teacher to mediate.
text.st: Morena Moshoeshoe I o re rutile: "Khotso ke khoro". Ha u ngangisana le motsoalle, khutlela morao, hema haholo hararo, bua ka mosa ’me u mamele lehlakore la hae. Ha ho hlokahala, kōpa tichere ho le ahlola.

text.en: Set up a "Peace Corner" (Khotso Corner) in the classroom where arguing learners sit to talk it out.
text.st: Thehang "Khutlo ea Khotso" phaposing moo bana ba neng ba qabana ba lulang ho buisana.

q.en: What was King Moshoeshoe I's famous motto regarding conflict and nation-building?
q.st: Ke lepetjo lefe le tummeng la Morena Moshoeshoe I mabapi le khotso le kaho ea sechaba?

title.en: Good Touch, Bad Touch, and Safe Secrets
title.st: Tšoaro e Ntle, Tšoaro e Mpe, le Liphiri tsa Tšireletseho

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Distinguish safe from unsafe touches and identify trusted adults for reporting
outcome.st: Khetholla tšoaro e ntle le e mpe le ho tseba batho ba baholo ba tšepahalang

lessons.source: Childline Lesotho / Child Protection and Welfare Act

text.en: Your body belongs to you alone. Private parts covered by swimming costumes or underwear must never be touched or photographed by anyone. If someone touches you in an uncomfortable way, shout "NO!", run away, and tell a trusted teacher or call Childline toll-free on 116.
text.st: ’Mele oa hao ke oa hao u le mong. Likarolo tsa sephiri tse koaheloang ke liaparo tsa ka hare ha lia lokela ho tšoaroa ke mang kapa mang. Haeba motho a u tšoara ka mokhoa o sa lokang, hoeletsa "CHEE!", baleha, ebe u bolella tichere kapa u letsetse Childline mahala ho 116.

text.en: Write the Childline Lesotho toll-free number (116) clearly on the board and have all learners memorize it.
text.st: Ngolang nomoro ea mahala ea Childline Lesotho (116) letlapeng baithuti bohle ba e tšoare ka hlooho.

q.en: What is the toll-free emergency phone number in Lesotho for child protection and reporting abuse (Childline)?
q.st: Ke nomoro efe ea mahala ea fono Lesotho ea tšireletso ea bana le ho tlaleha tlhekefetso (Childline)?

title.en: Standing Up Against Bullying and Teasing
title.st: Ho Ema Khahlanong le ho Tšeana le ho Hekefetsa

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Recognize bullying behavior (physical, verbal, exclusion) and practice being an upstander
outcome.st: Tseba mefuta ea tlhekefetso le ho ema le bana ba tlatlapuoang

text.en: Bullying is when someone repeatedly hurts, threatens, or makes fun of another person on purpose. It includes teasing someone because of their clothes, disability, or language. Bullying hurts minds and hearts. Be a friend who speaks up to protect classmates.
text.st: Tlhekefetso ke ha motho a lula a ntša e mong bohloko, a mo tšosa, kapa a mo tšeha ka boomo ka lebaka la liaparo, bofokoli kapa puo. Sena se utloisa bohloko haholo. E-ba motsoalle ea emang ho sireletsa ba bang.

text.en: Discuss the difference between being a passive bystander and being an active, compassionate defender.
text.st: Buisanang ka phapang pakeng tsa motho ea bohellang tlatlapo le ea thusang ho e thibela.

q.en: What should you do if you see bigger children picking on a smaller learner in the school yard?
q.st: U lokela ho etsa eng ha u bona bana ba baholo ba hlorisa ngoana e monyenyane lebaleng la sekolo?

options.en: Tell a teacher immediately or invite the child to join your group safely
options.st: Tsebisa tichere hang-hang kapa u bitse ngoana eo a tle sehlopheng sa heno

options.en: Cheer and join in teasing the child
options.st: Hooa ’me u kenelle ho mo tšeha

options.en: Film it on a phone and laugh

title.en: Caring for God’s Creation: Trees, Water, and Soil
title.st: Ho Hlokomela Tlholeho: Lifate, Metsi, le Mobu

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 4 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 4 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Connect personal spiritual responsibility to taking care of nature and water sources
outcome.st: Amanisa boikarabello ba moea le ho sireletsa mehloli ea metsi le tlhaho

text.en: Our mountains, clear rivers, and fertile fields are gifts of creation. When we dump plastic in streams, let taps run, or destroy trees, we harm ourselves and future generations. A wise Mosotho cares for the land with reverence and dignity.
text.st: Lithaba tsa rona, linoka tse hloekileng, le masimo a rona ke limpho tsa tlholeho. Ha re lahla lipolastiki linokeng, re senya metsi kapa re rema lifate, re ikgobatsa rona le meloko e tlang. Mosotho ea bohlale o hlokomela naha ka tlotla.

text.en: Organize a 10-minute classroom clean-up where learners collect and sort recyclable trash.
text.st: Etsang metsotso e 10 ea ho hloekisa lebala la sekolo le ho arola lithōle.

q.en: How can young learners practice good stewardship of natural water at home and school?
q.st: Bana ba ka bontša boikarabello bo botle joang tšebelisong ea metsi hae le sekolong?

options.en: Turn off dripping taps tightly and keep riverbanks free of trash
options.st: Koala lipompo tse rothang ka thata ’me u se ke oa silafatsa linoka

options.en: Leave taps running freely all night
options.st: Tlohela pompo e phalle bosiu bohle

options.en: Throw car batteries into village springs

title.en: Building Self-Confidence and Saying "No" to Peer Pressure
title.st: Ho Haha Boits'epo le ho Hana Khatello e Mpe ea Lithaka

syllabusRef.en: Flagged for School Verification: LCDC Grade 5 PSS Overview was not among the textbook photos (see Activity Plan gap note)
syllabusRef.st: E emetse ho netefatsoa ke sekolo: Leqephe la Sepheo sa PSS Sehlopha sa 5 le ne le sieo lifotong tsa libuka tsa sekolo

outcome.en: Demonstrate assertive communication when pressured into negative actions
outcome.st: Bontša boits'epo ba ho hana ha lithaka li u qobella ho etsa lintho tse mpe

text.en: Peer pressure happens when friends push you to do something dangerous or wrong (like stealing, skipping classes, or smoking) just to "fit in". A person with true self-esteem knows their values and says: "No, that is against my principles, and I will not do it."
text.st: Khatello ea lithaka e etsahala ha metsoalle e u susumelletsa ho etsa ntho e kotsi (joaloka ho utsoa, ho tlolela sekolo kapa ho tsuba) hore ba u nke u le "smart". Motho ea nang le boits'epo o tseba mekhoa ea hae ebe o re: "Che, ha ke etse ntho eo."

text.en: Practice assertive body language: standing tall, making direct eye contact, speaking in a firm, calm voice.
text.st: Koetlisang boemo ba ’mele bo tiileng: ho ema u otlolohile, ho sheba ka mahlong le ho bua ka lentsoe le tiileng.

q.en: If a group of friends dares you to skip school to hang around the shops, what is the most responsible response?
q.st: Haeba metsoalle e u qobella ho tlohela sekolo ho ea litoropong, karabo e nepahetseng ka ho fetisisa ke efe?

options.en: Firmly say "No, my education is important" and proceed to class
options.st: Bua ka tieo u re "Che, thuto ea ka ke ea bohlokoa" ebe u ea sekolong

options.en: Agree immediately so they don't call you names
options.st: Lumela hang-hang e le hore ba se u tšehe

options.en: Steal money from your parents to buy them sweets
options.st: Utsoa chelete ea batsoali u ba rekele lintho

title.st: Ho Tšehetsa Likhutsana le Bana ba Hlokang

syllabusRef.en: Flagged for School Verification: LCDC Grade 5 PSS Overview was not among the textbook photos (see Activity Plan gap note)
syllabusRef.st: E emetse ho netefatsoa ke sekolo: Leqephe la Sepheo sa PSS Sehlopha sa 5 le ne le sieo lifotong tsa libuka tsa sekolo

outcome.en: Cultivate empathy and practical solidarity with vulnerable children in the community
outcome.st: Hōlisa qenehelo le tšehetso e tiileng ho bana ba hlokang le likhutsana

text.en: In Lesotho, many children live with grandparents or have lost parents due to illness. They may lack warm jerseys, candles for studying, or enough food. Empathy means putting yourself in their shoes. Sharing textbooks, homework guidance, and friendship changes their world.
text.st: Lesotho, bana ba bangata ba lula le bo-nkhono kapa ba hlokahetsoe ke batsoali ke maloetse. Ba ka hloka lijase tse futhumetseng kapa lijo. Qenehelo e bolela ho ipona u le boemong ba bona. Ho ba fa botsoalle le ho ba thusa mesebetsing ea sekolo ho fetola bophelo ba bona.

text.en: Encourage a classroom study buddy system pairing learners for homework support.
text.st: Hlophisang lithaka tsa ho ithuta phaposing moo bana ba phelang hammoho ho thusana ka homework.

q.en: What is the most respectful way to support a classmate who has no school shoes in winter?
q.st: Ke tsela efe e nang le tlhompho ea ho tšehetsa moithuti-’moho ea se nang lieta tsa sekolo mariha?

options.en: Quietly inform the teacher or school welfare committee with dignity and kindness
options.st: Tsebisa tichere kapa komiti ea boiketlo ea sekolo ka tlhompho le boikokobetso

options.en: Point at their feet in the assembly and laugh
options.st: Mo supe ka menwana phuthehong u tšehe

options.en: Take photos and post them online
options.st: Mo nke lifoto u li phatlalatse

title.en: Freedom of Worship and Respecting Different Faiths
title.st: Tokoloho ea Thapelo le Tlhompho ea Malumeli a Fapaneng

syllabusRef.en: Flagged for School Verification: LCDC Grade 5 PSS Overview was not among the textbook photos (see Activity Plan gap note)
syllabusRef.st: E emetse ho netefatsoa ke sekolo: Leqephe la Sepheo sa PSS Sehlopha sa 5 le ne le sieo lifotong tsa libuka tsa sekolo

outcome.en: Demonstrate respect and tolerance for people of different religious and spiritual backgrounds
outcome.st: Bontša mamello le tlhompho ho batho ba malumeli a fapaneng

text.en: Under the Constitution of Lesotho, every person has the right to freedom of religion and conscience. Whether someone belongs to the LECSA, Catholic, Anglican, Methodist, Muslim, or traditional heritage, we treat their spiritual beliefs with honor and tolerance.
text.st: Tlas'a Molao oa Motheo oa Lesotho, motho e mong le e mong o na le tokelo ea bolokolohi ba bolumeli. Ho sa tsotellehe hore na motho ke oa Kereke ea Fora (LECSA), Roma, Chache, Methodist, kapa Mo-Islam, re tšoara tumelo ea hae ka tlhompho le mamello.

text.en: Emphasize the universal spiritual values shared across faiths: love, peace, honesty, and justice.
text.st: Totobatsang litekanyetso tsa moea tse kopanyang malumeli: lerato, khotso, botšepehi, le toka.

q.en: What fundamental freedom is protected in Lesotho regarding how citizens pray and worship?
q.st: Ke tokelo efe ea bohlokoa e sirelelitsoeng Lesotho mabapi le kamoo baahi ba rapelang kateng?

options.en: Freedom of religion, conscience, and peaceful worship for all
options.st: Tokelo ea bolokolohi ba bolumeli, letsoalo, le thapelo bakeng sa bohle

options.en: Only one church is allowed to exist by law
options.st: Kereke e le 'ngoe feela e lumelletsoeng

options.en: Citizens are forced to change religions every year
options.st: Batho ba qobelloa ho fetola malumeli selemo le selemo

topic.st: Mamello ea Maikutlo le ho Laola Khatello

title.en: Managing School Stress and Exam Anxiety
title.st: Ho Laola Matšoenyeho a Litlhahlobo le Khatello

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Apply constructive stress coping strategies (study planning, rest, mindful breathing)
outcome.st: Sebelisa mekhoa e metle ea ho laola matšoenyeho a litlhahlobo le mosebetsi

text.en: Preparing for examinations or facing difficult home situations can create stress and anxiety. Good ways to cope include drawing up a daily study timetable, taking short breaks, getting enough sleep, and talking openly with a school mentor.
text.st: Ho itokisetsa litlhahlobo kapa mathata a lapeng ho ka baka matšoenyeho le khatello ea kelello. Mekhoa e metle ea ho sebetsana le sena e kenyeletsa ho etsa lenaneo la ho ithuta, ho phomola, ho robala hantle, le ho bua le tichere kapa moeletsi.

text.en: Lead a 2-minute box-breathing exercise: inhale for 4 counts, hold for 4, exhale for 4, rest for 4.
text.st: Etsang boikoetliso ba ho hema: hema ka lipalo tse 4, tšoara moea tse 4, ntša moea tse 4, phomola tse 4.

q.en: Which habit is most effective for reducing examination panic and anxiety before test day?
q.st: Ke tloaelo efe e thusang haholo ho fokotsa letsoalo pele ho litlhahlobo?

options.en: Revising lessons steadily weeks in advance and getting adequate rest
options.st: Ho boela lithuto butle-butle libeke pele ho nako le ho robala hantle

options.en: Staying awake all night drinking strong energy drinks
options.st: Ho lula bosiu bohle u sa robale

options.en: Skipping meals and avoiding all study notes
options.st: Ho itima lijo le ho se bale ho hang

title.en: Promoting Gender Equality Between Boys and Girls
title.st: Ho Khothaletsa Tekano Pakeng tsa Bashanyana le Banana

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Challenge harmful gender stereotypes and promote equal leadership and educational dignity
outcome.st: Hlōla mekhoa e kentseng khethollo ea bong le ho khothaletsa boetapele bo lekanang

lessons.source: Lesotho National Gender and Development Policy

text.en: Both girls and boys have equal intelligence, leadership capacity, and human rights. Outdated beliefs that domestic chores belong only to girls or that boys cannot express feelings harm everyone. In schools and homes, sharing tasks and respecting each other builds a just society.
text.st: Banana le bashanyana ba na le bohlale bo lekanang, bokhoni ba boetapele, le litokelo tsa botho. Menahano ea khale ea hore mesebetsi ea lapeng ke ea banana feela kapa hore bashanyana ha ba lle e senya sechaba. Ho arolelana mesebetsi ho haha naha e lokileng.

text.en: Assign classroom leadership and cleaning tasks on an equal rotation regardless of gender.
text.st: Abang mesebetsi ea boetapele le bohloeki phaposing ka ho fapanyetsana ntle le khethollo ea bong.

q.en: Why is it important for both boys and girls to have equal access to mathematics, science, and leadership roles?
q.st: Hobaneng ha ho le bohlokoa hore bashanyana le banana ba be le menyetla e lekanang lipalong, saenseng le boetapeleng?

options.en: Because a prosperous nation needs the talents, ideas, and skills of all its citizens
options.st: Hobane naha e tsoetseng pele e hloka talenta le bokhoni ba baahi bohle

options.en: Because girls are only allowed to do cooking
options.st: Hobane banana ba tšoanela ho pheha feela

options.en: Because boys are not allowed to read books
options.st: Hobane bashanyana ha baa lokela ho bala

title.st: Mosebetsi oa Boithaopo le Tšebeletso ea Sechaba

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 6 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 6 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Demonstrate civic commitment through voluntary community action
outcome.st: Bontša boitlamo sechabeng ka mesebetsi ea boithaopo (letsema)

text.en: Volunteering (boithaopo) means giving your time and energy to help your community without expecting payment. Traditionally, Basotho practiced "letsema" to weed fields or build homes. Serving your community strengthens social bonds and develops leadership skills.
text.st: Boithaopo bo bolela ho fana ka nako le matla a hao ho thusa sechaba ntle le tefo. Moetlong oa khale, Basotho ba ne ba etsa "letsema" ho lema kapa ho haha matlo. Ho sebeletsa sechaba sa heno ho tiisa lerato le ho haha boetapele bo botle.

text.en: Plan a small school volunteer initiative (cleaning the community spring or helping an elderly villager stack firewood).
text.st: Ralang mosebetsi o monyenyane oa boithaopo: ho hloekisa seliba sa motse kapa ho rala patsi ea nkhono.

q.en: What traditional Basotho community practice embodies the spirit of collective volunteerism and mutual aid?
q.st: Ke moetlo ofe oa Sesotho o emelang moea oa boithaopo le ho thusana ka kakaretso?

topic.st: Thibelo ea Tšebeliso e Mpe ea Lithethefatsi

title.en: Saying NO to Alcohol, Tobacco, and Drugs
title.st: Ho Hana Joala, Koae, le Lithethefatsi

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Analyze the physical, mental, and social consequences of substance abuse
outcome.st: Hlahloba litlamorao tsa ’mele, kelello le sechaba tsa tšebeliso ea lithethefatsi

lessons.source: Lesotho National Drug and Alcohol Policy / Health Curriculum

text.en: Substance abuse damages the developing brain, ruins academic futures, and leads to addiction, violence, and disease. Making healthy lifestyle choices, choosing positive friendships, and focusing on education protects your dreams and physical well-being.
text.st: Tšebeliso e mpe ea lithethefatsi (joala, koae, matekoane) e senya boko bo holang, e bolaea bokamoso ba thuto, ’me e baka bokhoba le bokuli. Ho etsa liqeto tse nepahetseng le ho khetha metsoalle e metle ho sireletsa litoro tsa hao.

text.en: Discuss refusal skills: clearly saying "I have goals that drugs would ruin" and walking away.
text.st: Rutang mekhoa ea ho hana: "Che, ke na le litoro tseo lithethefatsi li ka li senyang."

q.en: What is a severe long-term danger of alcohol and substance abuse among adolescents?
q.st: Ke kotsi efe e kholo ea nako e telele ea tšebeliso ea joala le lithethefatsi har'a bacha?

options.en: Permanent brain damage, addiction, and school dropout
options.st: Tšenyo ea boko, bokhoba ba lithethefatsi, le ho tlohela sekolo

options.en: Achieving the highest marks in national exams
options.st: Ho fumana lintlha tse holimo litlhahlobong
Ho ba semathi se potlakileng sa lithaba

title.en: Responsible Phone Use and Protecting Online Privacy
title.st: Tšebeliso e Ntle ea Mehala le Tšireletso ea Sephiri

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Practice safe, respectful online behavior and avoid cyberbullying and scam traps
outcome.st: Sebelisa mehala le marang-rang ka boikarabello, tlhompho, le tšireletso

text.en: Smartphones and digital media are powerful tools for learning, but they come with risks. Never share your passwords, home address, or private photos with strangers online. Avoid forwarding mean gossip or fake news on WhatsApp or social media. Treat people with the same Botho online as face-to-face.
text.st: Mehala le marang-rang ke lisebelisoa tse matla tsa ho ithuta, empa li na le likotsi. Le ka mohla u se ke oa arolelana liphasewete kapa lifoto tsa sephiri le batho bao u sa ba tsebeng. Qoba ho romella litaba tsa leshano le ho rohaka ba bang ho WhatsApp. Bontša Botho marang-rang joaloka sefahleho le sefahleho.

text.en: Directly relate this to Moshoeshoe Hub app: an example of ethical technology that protects privacy by collecting zero user data.
text.st: Amanisang sena le Moshoeshoe Hub: mohlala oa theknoloji e nang le boitšoaro e sa bokelleng litaba tsa sephiri tsa bana.

q.en: What should you do if an unknown stranger on WhatsApp or social media asks for your home address or private photos?
q.st: U lokela ho etsa eng haeba motho eo u sa mo tsebeng ho WhatsApp a u kopa aterese ea heno kapa linepe tsa sephiri?

options.en: Block the number immediately and report it to a parent or teacher
options.st: Mo thibele hang-hang (block) ebe u bolella motsoali kapa tichere

options.en: Send them your photos and address right away
options.st: Mo romelle linepe le aterese hang-hang

options.en: Meet them in a dark lonely place alone
options.st: Kopana le eena sebakeng se lefifi u le mong

title.en: Setting Life Goals and Transitioning to High School
title.st: Ho Rala Lipheo le ho Itokisetsa Sekolo se Phahameng

syllabusRef.en: Lesotho MOET / LCDC Primary Curriculum · Grade 7 · Personal, Spiritual & Social Learning Area (PSS)
syllabusRef.st: Lenaneo la Thuto la Lesotho (LCDC) · Sehlopha sa 7 · Personal, Spiritual & Social (PSS)

outcome.en: Formulate personal academic goals and prepare emotionally for secondary education
outcome.st: Rala lipheo tsa thuto le ho itokisetsa sekolo se phahameng ka boits'epo

text.en: Completing primary school (Grade 7) is a proud milestone. Transitioning to high school requires independence, strong study discipline, and clear vision. Write down your goals, choose friendships that elevate you, and remember that with perseverance, education unlocks your destiny.
text.st: Ho qeta sekolo sa motheo (Grade 7) ke katleho e kholo ea boikhohomoso. Ho fetela sekolong se phahameng ho hloka boikemelo, boikarabello, le pono e hlakileng. Ngola fatše lipheo tsa hao, khetha metsoalle e u phahamisang, ’me u hopole hore thuto e bula menyako eohle ea bophelo.

text.en: Have each Grade 7 learner write a letter to their future self in 5 years describing who they want to become.
text.st: Kopang moithuti ka mong ho ngolla "eena oa bokamoso" lengolo le hlalosang toro ea hae ka lilemo tse 5 tse tlang.

q.en: What personal trait is most essential for overcoming academic challenges as you transition to secondary school?
q.st: Ke boleng bofe ba motho bo bohlokoa ka ho fetisisa ho hlōla mathata a thuto ha u kena sekolong se phahameng?

options.en: Perseverance (Mamello), self-discipline, and consistent hard work
options.st: Mamello, boikarabello, le ho sebetsa ka thata ho tsoelang pele

options.en: Giving up the first time a question is difficult
options.st: Ho tela hang ha potso e le thata
